posts.caption:
What does it look like to take engineering beyond the classroom? For 12 #BaskinEngineering students, it meant connecting with thousands of engineers and industry professionals at the Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers (SHPE) National Convention in Indianapolis. 

SHPE is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Hispanic and Latino students and professionals in STEM. UCSC’s chapter (@shpe.ucsc) is part of the Baskin Engineering community and creates opportunities for students to build connections, develop leadership skills, and support one another as they pursue careers in engineering. 💛

For UCSC SHPE President Leilah-louise Cuenca, the convention offered a closer look at careers as a biomolecular engineering major.

"I learned a lot about what a day looks like in R&D, as well as how cross-functional teams collaborate to develop life-saving technology and medicine," she said. "I aim to use what I learned to shape my next steps of exploring biomolecular engineering from an industry perspective."

👏 The opportunity was made possible by the chapter's SHPE Nationals Funding Committee, which raised more than $15,000 to fully fund all 12 students' attendance.

📸 Image descriptions:
1- UCSC SHPE President Leilah-Louise Cuenca stands beside a Mexican flag, with flags from other countries displayed behind her.
2- Top: Students pose in front of a large “FAMILIA” sign at the conference. Bottom: Students pose in front of a “SHPEtinas” banner.
3- UCSC SHPE students pose together at the Indianapolis airport.

[SHPE is open to all students consistent with state and federal law, the UC Nondiscrimination Statement and the Nondiscrimination Policy Statement for University of California Publications Regarding Student-Related Matters]

posts.caption:
Hey UCSC Students, Friends, and Families!! TIS THE SEASON FOR SOME GIVING!! 

Bayanihan at UCSC is a student-led organization that aims to cultivate unity, empowerment, and advocacy for the Pilipinx student body. It strives to be a cultural resource for the Pilipinx community, but also it’s open to everyone, regardless if you’re Pilipinx or not. 

We, as an organization, were successful in raising $3370 on Giving Day for last year’s PCC XXXV. These funds are going to this year’s PCC XXXVI that will happen in Spring Quarter! To encourage folks to donate, we compiled a list of fun and silly dares that Bayanihan Core will participate in after reaching a certain donation threshold!

With your help, we can elevate our stories and continue Bayanihan’s history and legacy for years to come. Share with your communities! Anything helps! Donation link will be as a QR code in this post AND in our bio!

Love, 
The Bayanihan Community

¡Hola, comunidad! 🌹Save the Date! Giving Day is November 18th! Support MEChA de UCSC as we bring our comunidad together and continue building spaces rooted in solidarity and collective care! Thank you for being part of our community and supporting us!

Your donations will support:
🪧 Local Unions: Uplifting service workers and supporting efforts to improve working conditions.
🚌 MEChA National Conference: Helping students cover transportation, lodging, and meals.
🌯 Weekly Colectivas: Funding food, supplies, and materials for political education and community-building.
🤝 Mutual Aid: Providing resources, food, and direct support to students and community members.
💓 EVERY DONATION COUNTS! Whether it’s $1, $5, $10, or $25, no contribution is too small.
#give2ucsc #UCSC #GivingDay #MEChAdeUCSC

Image description: A burgundy-and-cream flyer featuring a group photo of MEChA de UCSC members gathered in front of a community ofrenda. The photo is framed with a decorative white lace border. Below the photo, the flyer reads “Save the Date: Giving Day, Nov. 18th.” A message to the community reads:” Your generosity helps MEChA de UCSC continue creating spaces for cultura, community, and opportunities! Help us keep our communidad growing, and thank you for supporting!” The MEChA de UCSC logo is displayed in the bottom right corner.

posts.caption:
Meet the council...

John (he/him) is our wonderful Music Director for this year. Though he sings bass, John is spends most of his time as vocal percussionist for the group. He is also currently a 4th year Computer Science major!

Alongside John is Mac (he/him), this year's Assistant Music Director. With a versatile, rich voice, Mac helps to lead our Tenor section! Academically, he's a 3rd year studying Global and Community Health.

Elise (she/her) is our fabulous, talented, incredible, intelligent (the list continues...) President. Truly the glue that holds us together and keeps us all on track. She is an alto and currently in her 3rd year of her Neuroscience major!

Finally we have Jayna (they/he), our PR for this year. A member of our soprano section, they are currently a 2nd year majoring in Biochemistry! (.❛ ᴗ ❛.)

Not only that, but Jovani is also almost always ready for a gardening session, helping to keep the true essence of Cloud 9 alive 🍃 ;)

posts.caption:
Happy Key Friendship Friday from Marissa and Adeline! 🗝️🩵 Read below messages they wrote for each other 🫶💌 

Dear Adeline, 
From the moment I met you and we took turns hyping each other up while taking pics at the beach on cob bid night, I knew we were bound to be best friends.  From that moment on, you never stopped lifting me up and making me a better version of myself. From our first carpool to our first sisterhood, to the free poke bowls you give me, to the late night chats we have - either over text, FaceTime, or in one of our rooms, I cherish each and every moment we get to spend together. I am so lucky to call you my twin and I truly feel like we get one another on that level. You are literally my mind reader. I love how silly we can be with one another and I love the copious amounts of photos of us in my camera roll. I also have so much fun stealing your clothes and seeing you borrow mine because we are twins and we share a closet. I can’t wait to make more memories with you in the future!!! Thank you for being such a ray of sunshine, I love you! 
Xoxo, Missy 

Marissa,
i knew from the moment i met you that we were meant to be friends. but i never could have guessed how ingrained into my life you would become. from sleepovers to coffee debriefs to everything in between, there’s no one i would rather call my twin. shoutout addie for picking us both up, because i couldn’t imagine my college experience without you. i’ve never met someone so similar to me, we get excited about the same things, anxious about the same things and weird about the same things. you always get me and i know i can always turn to you for a shoulder to cry on or for a good laugh. i can’t wait for the new memories that we’ll make, and i’ll always cherish the ones we have. 
Love, Adeline 

#ucsckkg #keyfriendshipfriday #kkg

¡Hola, comunidad! 🌹We are halfway into pre-donating, but your support still matters! There is still time to pre-donate and support MEChA de UCSC this Giving Day. Every contribution helps us continue building community, supporting our students, and building spaces rooted in solidarity and collective care! Thank you for being part of our comunidad! 🫶🏽

Your donations will support:
🪧 Local Unions: Uplifting service workers and supporting efforts to improve working conditions.
🚌 MEChA National Conference: Helping students cover transportation, lodging, and meals.
🌯 Weekly Colectivas: Funding food, supplies, and materials for political education and community-building.
🤝 Mutual Aid: Providing resources, food, and direct support to students and community members.
💓 EVERY DONATION COUNTS! Whether it’s $1, $5, $10, or $25, no contribution is too small.
#give2ucsc #UCSC #GivingDay #MEChAdeUCSC

Image description: A Giving Day promotional flyer for MEChA de UCSC with a light pink textured background and a retro-computer-style design. At the top, bold black lettering reads, HALFWAY THERE, YOUR SUPPORT STILL MATTERS!” The flyer features a collage of photographs highlighting MEChA’s community, events, tabling, and students’ involvement. A digital notes window lists reminders to pre-donate, support MEChA de UCSC, and to remember to donate. Below the collage, a computer-style progress bar reads “Pre-donating progress loading…” with a Giving Day label. A smaller group photo appears also alongside a MEChA label below. A MEChA de UCSC logo is located in the bottom-right corner.

¡Hola Laso Communidad! 

If you don’t already know Giving Day starting November 18th is UC Santa Cruz’s largest fundraising event of the year, bringing together students, alumni, families, friends, and community members to support the programs and organizations that make a difference on campus

Why donate to LaSo?

This Giving Day, your support helps us create more opportunities for Latine students pursuing a future in the legal field! From law school field trips and networking events to professional development workshops and LSAT preparation, every contribution helps us provide valuable resources and build a stronger, more supportive community.

Your generosity helps make these opportunities possible and supports the next generation of Latine legal professionals. Every donation makes a difference!

Donate on November 18 by scanning the QR code or visiting the link in our bio!

Thank you for supporting LaSo and helping us continue our mission. ¡Muchas gracias! 💙💛

Your Allied Rapid Response for Santa Cruz County (YARR) confirmed ICE agents’ presence at about 5:30 p.m. on Water and Ocean streets near the Santa Cruz Jail. Witnesses reported multiple ICE agents, though the number is not specified. Witnesses also reported four ICE vehicles in the area. As of 5:38 p.m., the ICE agents and vehicles are still reported to be in the area near the Santa Cruz Jail. 

La organización Your Allied Rapid Response (YARR) para el condado de Santa Cruz confirmó la presencia de agentes de ICE a las 5:30 p.m., en la calle de Water y Ocean, cerca a la cárcel del condado de Santa Cruz. Los testigos informaron a múltiples agentes de ICE. También los testigos informaron cuatro carros en el área. A las 5:38 p.m., se informa que los agentes de ICE y los carros todavía se encuentran en el área cerca de la cárcel del condado de Santa Cruz. 

Photographs of their vehicles can be found on YARR’s Facebook and Instagram yarr.scc 

Puedes encontrar fotos de los carros en las páginas de Facebook e Instagram de YARR.

posts.caption:
¡Hola comunidad 🌹Here is what we are fundraising for this year!

Support MEChA de UCSC as we bring our comunidad together and continue building spaces rooted in solidarity and collectivity. We are participating in the Headstart Challenge taking place from November 4th to 17th, so you don’t gotta wait until the 18th to donate! The team with the most unique donors during Early Giving period (Nov 4th-17th) will receive additional funding!!

Your donations will support:
🪧 Local Unions: Uplifting service workers and supporting efforts to improve working conditions.
🚌 MEChA National Conference: Helping students cover transportation, lodging, and meals.
🌯 Weekly Colectivas: Funding food, supplies, and materials for political education and community-building.
🤝 Mutual Aid: Providing resources, food, and direct support to students and community members.

💓 EVERY DONATION COUNTS! Whether it’s $1, $5, $10, or $25, no contribution is too small.
#give2ucsc #ucscgiving #ucsc #MEChAdeUCSC #MEChA

Image description: A Giving Day 2026 flyer for MEChA de UCSC that features a burgundy and muted pink color scheme with the MEChA eagle logo at the top. The flyer highlights several ways donations support the organization, including promoting political education and culturally relevant events; strengthening mutual aid; supporting local unions and workers; providing food and supplies for weekly Colectivas; and helping MEChistas attend the National MEChA Conference to develop leadership and organizational skills. The flyer emphasizes that every donation helps sustain the MEChA community. It also includes information on how to donate through the link in MEChA’s bio or at bit.ly/Give2MECHAdeUCSC.

posts.caption:
I am here to officially announce that GDA is participating in...💸 GIVING DAY !!! 💸 
>> Giving Day is an annual event where students, alumni, parents, and others can easily send a direct donation to student organizations they would like to help. If you want to support GDA, today through the 18th will be the time to do so!
───
Please consider visiting our to help us give back to this wonderful community!
✨ For this round of Giving Day, GDA will be participating in the **Head Start challenge** —where the team with the highest number of donors during the early giving day period (Nov 4-17)  will get a bonus cash award— so just donating $5 will still be appreciated!!

All donations we receive through Giving Day will go towards the club. Funds will help us buy supplies, host events (by paying for food and venues), and more! 

[ pssst and don’t worry, you too, will get an award from donating to us ] 
───
Thank you for the donations over the last 8 days; your support will always be appreciated 💚 
Because of your support, we were able to hit tier 2 of our goal!! This means that bidding for the GDA-chan cutout is now UNLOCKED !! The highest bidder will get the previous cutout!!
───
A reminder to have your donation public so that we can contact you for your prizes after Giving Day!!!
#Give2UCSC #UCSC #UCSCgda #GivingDay2026 #UCSCGivingDay

posts.caption:
Hello Everyone, A reminder that Giving Day is November 18th! Ways you can support our organization on Giving Day is by donating and sharing our socials to friends, family, and peers. Especially by liking and spreading this post! ⋆˚꩜｡

On giving day there will be hourly challenges and CORE will have our own dares that we have already posted! Make sure to be on the look out for any other updates!

We greatly appreciate the support! 🫶🏼
#give2ucsc 
ucsc 

Con amor,
Los Mejicas ♡

Translation: 

Hola a todos, un recordatorio que día de donación es el 18 de Noviembre! Formas que puedes apoyar a nuestra organización en el día de la donación es donando y compartiendo nuestras páginas sociales a familiares y amigos. Especialmente por dar un like y compartiendo esta publicación! 

En el día de donación vamos a estar participando en desafíos de cada hora y miembros de CORE participarán en sus propios desafíos que ya hemos publicado! Estén atentos a cualquier otra actualización! 

Apreciamos mucho el apoyo! 🫶🏼

⊹ ࣪ ˖ Por Qué Deberían Donar A Los Mejicas En El Día De Donación ⊹ ࣪ ˖

಄Vestuario ಄

Con sus donaciones podremos a comprar vestuario nuevo como zapatos, joyería, tocados de pelo, vestidos y mucho más! También vamos a poder mantener, reparar, y remplazar vestuario viejo o dañado.

಄Presentaciones ಄

Con sus donaciones podremos a financiar presentaciones durante el año! Por ejemplo, Danzantes Unidos es una des las presentaciones más importantes que la mayor parte de fondos va para. Con sus donaciones podemos hacer posible ser parte de este evento y muchos más! 

಄Espectáculo De Primavera ಄

Nuestro espectáculo de primavera annual es donde mostramos las regiones de México que hemos aprendido durante el año escolar! Con sus donaciones podremos mostrar nuestro trabajo y representar nuestra cultura a familiares, amigos, y comunidad!

posts.caption:
Support the 2027 UCSC iGEM team! 

DONATE AT THIS LINK: 
https://give.ucsc.edu/schools/UniversityofCaliforniaSantaCruz/giving-day-2026/pages/igem-2027/

Each year, UCSC assembles a team of 15-20 undergraduate researchers to push the boundaries of synthetic biology by designing, building, testing, and measuring genetically engineered systems to tackle real-world problems. We participate in the iGEM Competition, an annual synthetic biology conference where teams from all over the globe come together present their work to a panel of judges.

In the past, our student researchers have worked on projects tackling harmful Lyme disease bacteria, toxic algal blooms, type II diabetes, accessible birth control, and bioenergy. Beyond the lab, our outreach includes going to local Santa Cruz schools to present research in synthetic biology and lead hands-on projects such as DNA extraction.

This year, your gift helps us build on our research and outreach efforts by funding laboratory materials and travel expenses needed to share our ideas with the scientific community!

Get a head start on supporting our upcoming project by donating NOW until November 18th. You can also support us on UCSC’s Giving Day, November 18th, starting at 12:00 AM and running until 11:59 PM.

#igem #ucscgivingday #ucsc #baskinengineering

Happy Why Kappa Wednesday! Hear from roommates Lily Kopf, MC ‘25 and Izzy Choi, MC ‘26. 

“Hi!! My name is Lily and I joined kappa fall 2025! When I first joined Kappa I instantly felt at home after meeting the most loving girls! I can’t imagine my college experience without Kappa. I’ve truly found the most amazing girls through this sorority, including my favorite roommates and girls who make me laugh harder than anyone else. I’m so so grateful for these lifelong friendships and I can’t wait to make more memories with my Kappas! 🩵”

“Hi! My name is Izzy and I joined kappa this year during fall recruitment! I was nervous going in as a sophomore, but all the girls I met were so welcoming and sweet. I chose Kappa because of the strong mental health philanthropy and the sisterhood! I feel so grateful to be apart of a group of girls who support each other and I know I can always count on. I’ve already made so many memories and I can’t wait to spend the next few years with my sisters!”

#kkg #wkw #ucsc

posts.caption:
Written by Isabel White and Reggie Sasaki
Illustration by Mikayla Palmquist

As much as we wish it weren’t so, artificial intelligence has hit the journalism industry. 

While scouring the internet for articles on the subject, we were bombarded with various headlines praising the technology as the industry’s newest, always-available, all-knowing assistant. Though news sites originally appeared to be an oasis of critical AI sentiment, we clicked on a piece by The Media Copilot, titled “Journalism’s workforce shrinks as AI and new consumer habits reshape the industry.” 

Read more the link in our bio.

posts.caption:
Do you identify as LGBTQIA? Growing up did you struggle to accept your identity or feel rejected because of who you loved? If so, you are invited to participate in a research study about your experiences conducted by a researcher who identifies as queer!

Eligibility:
18+
Self-identify as sexual and/or gender diverse
Self-identify as having adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) “potentially traumatic events that occur in childhood (0-17 years)”. 

If you meet the eligibility criteria, click this link or check out the attached flyer to sign up for a 1 hour in person interview (conducted by a researcher who identifies as queer) and answer questions about both positive and negative childhood experiences.

If you have questions about the study feel free to contact Eva Hellmold (ekhellmo@ucsc.edu).

This study has been approved by the IRB.
Study #HS-FY2026-316
University of California, Santa Cruz
1156 High St, Santa Cruz, CA 95064 

Please forward this study to anyone you think may be interested in participating. I would also greatly appreciate your help sharing the attached flyer or survey link with friends, peers, or other folks who may be interested in participating.

This study is open to all LGBTQIA+ experiences but if you know of any BIPOC LGBTQIA+ folks who meet the eligibility requirements, I would especially appreciate you sharing the study with them.

Thank you so much for considering participating and for any help you can provide in sharing the study! To learn more about the study visit the Adverse Childhood Experiences, Sexuality, & Gender website to view FAQs, resources, and the research team.

posts.caption:
FILM-185X: EyeCandy Seminar Applications ARE NOW OPEN!! 👁️🍬👁️🍬👁️🍬 There are two paths you can take when joining our class: 

Writing Path: Students will write a ~1,500-word article for our journal published in spring. Along the way, they’ll receive feedback on structure/flow, analysis of chosen material, incorporation of research, and ability to write for a leisurely audience as opposed to an academic one. This feedback will be given by the writing editors as well as through other students in class.
Design Path: Students will design a 4-5 page spread for 1 article (written by other students) to be published in spring. They will learn Adobe’s InDesign software to incorporate graphics and effects related to the article’s contents and cohesive to the overall theme of the magazine. Group discussions of the work will help to improve upon skills relating to InDesign as well as design techniques as a whole.

FILM-185X EyeCandy Seminar is a 5 credit course, a Film and Digital Media Upper Division Elective, and a PR-C General Education course. There are no prerequisites to taking this course, you all are welcome to apply for enrollment! 👁️🍬

posts.caption:
How did your dollars make a difference for Formula Slug? Let’s look at the impact of Giving Day 2025 💙💛

Formula Slug is UC Santa Cruz’s premier student-run electric vehicle team, competing each June in the international Formula SAE Electric competition in Michigan.

Last Giving Day, Formula Slug raised $47,807 from 1,010 donors. These funds launched a new software subsystem to debut their first autonomous car, formed dedicated aerodynamics and composites teams, and covered cross-country logistics to get the vehicle to national competitions.

Giving Day at UC Santa Cruz is a 24-hour fundraising campaign that has occurred every year since 2015. Thousands of Slugs and their supporters unite annually to support scholarships, groundbreaking research, student clubs, athletics teams, resource centers, and more. The 10th annual Giving Day hosted more than 200 project teams and raised $1.98 million for participating campus programs and student organizations. 

Make a difference and give to a cause you care about this Giving Day—November 18, 2026.

Learn more at the link in bio.

📸 Image descriptions:
1- Students in yellow team shirts pushing a racecar. Text: “You made an impact on Formula Slug.”
2- A student sitting in a racecar at a racetrack. Text: “Formula Slug is UC Santa Cruz’s premier student-run electric vehicle team, competing each June in the international Formula SAE Electric competition in Michigan.”
3- A student working in the shop. Text: “‘Being part of Formula Slug has had a dramatic, transformative effect on my UC Santa Cruz experience. I’ve found a greater purpose and motivation that encourages me to work harder and strive for greater things, and Formula Slug is at the heart of it all.’ — Max Simonen Luke (Cowell ’27)”
4- Group photo of students standing around race car. Text: “Impact by Numbers Formula Slug - Total raised: $47,807 Total donors: 1,010”

(Image descriptions continued in comments)

posts.caption:
Explore some of our favorite directors and zine publications in our weekly Director/Zine Spotlights! This week we focus on Jean-Pierre Jeunet and Femicide Zine.‧⁺˚*･༓☾

Jean-Pierre Jeunet is a renowned french director and screenwriter famous for his highly stylized and surreal visual aesthetic. He is most known for his film, Amélie (2001), which landed him in BBC’s 100 greatest films of the 21st century. He has also directed Delicatessen (1991), La Cité des Enfants Perdus (1995), A Very Long Engagement (2004), Alien:Resurrection (1997), and various animated films, music videos, and ads. 

Founded by Imarni Boyer-Nugent in 2021, Femicide Zine is a UK based intersectional feminist, alternative art, and music zine rooted in 90s Riot Grrrl culture. It runs as a submission-based publication and each issue is wholly unique with no set design or style to encourage complete creative freedom for each iteration. They print physical zines as well as upload digital copies on their website which you can access through their bio.

posts.caption:
On the 13th year anniversary of Super Typhoon Haiyan making rainfall in the Philippines, youth and students from Kabataan Alliance in NorCal and Bayanihan at UCSC echo the calls to shut down Pax Silica!

Super Typhoon Haiyan was one of the most catastrophic typhoons to hit the Philippines leaving about 6,300 casualties, over 1,000 missing, and thousands of families still displaced especially across poor communities, the peasant farmer and fisherfolk neighborhoods, and in the Eastern Visayas region. We also recognize that it was after such a devastating typhoon that started Kabataan Alliance, because the Filipino youth across the diaspora refuse to be silent amidst corruption ever so prevalent in their communities. 

We continue to refuse to remain silent when our migrants are being attacked by the Trump administration, when corrupt officials steal taxes from the Filipino people for ghost flood control projects in 2025, when the Armed Forces of the Philippines continue to militarize provinces in the archipelago, and most especially when the Philippine and US government collude to prioritize AI development in the Philippines through projects that will harm the lives, land, and livelihood of Indigenous People’s and peasant farmers. 

On November 16-18, US President Donald Trump will be visiting the Philippines to potentially sign Pax Silica into notion. Join us in the national day of action on November 16th in Northern California against Trump’s visit and in the fight to shut down Pax Silica!

posts.caption:
GPHI ABROAD ✈️🩷 with our sister Isabella! 

For the past quarter, Isabella has been studying abroad in Barcelona, Spain! Here’s what she has to say about her experience: 

“I’ve been studying abroad in Barcelona, Spain, and it has been such a lovely experience. I’ve loved getting to know the culture of Catalonia, exploring the streets of Barcelona, trying new foods, and traveling to places across Europe. Getting to experience so many different cultures, meet new people, and see new places has been so wonderful. It has also been very special living with roommates and having people from Santa Cruz here in Barcelona.Having a little piece of home with me while experiencing somewhere new has made this experience even more meaningful.”

#gammaphibeta #gphi #panhellenic

“Hi everyone, my name is Makayla and I am studying broad this quarter in Rome, Italy! I have absolutely loved my time being abroad in Rome! Through studying abroad I have been able to experience to much, meet so many new, amazing people, travel to beautiful places and experience some amazing cultures. So far through my time studying abroad I would have to say my favorite memory so far has been going to the Italian Dolomites! The mountains and Dolomites were so beautiful and breathtaking while also got to see Venice along the way! I got to go with all of my roommates that I’ve met here, and create some amazing memories I will never forget! I am so excited to continue my time in Italy and am very grateful to study in such a beautiful place! 🇮🇹❤️”

We can’t wait for you to come home Makayla💌

Our campaign is live! Link in bio & story highlights. 

The Eloise Pickard Smith gallery believes in the ability of art to enhance one’s everyday life. One way for us to do so is to host a series of workshops called Art Fridays throughout the academic year. 
Materials are provided in these free workshops, and all students are welcome regardless of their level of experience and major. 
Art Friday is student-led programming that ties the exhibition on display to a hands-on workshop. Every week, the Art Friday intern leads students through the making of an art practice that relates to the current exhibition on display. It’s programming for students by students. 
The funding we seek to raise is to support the wage for the student intern leading Art Fridays and the cost of materials.

#give2ucsc

Every day of the week, “A” is a residential assistant (RA) at Porter/Kresge College. In addition, A works eight to nine hours a week as a global peer advisor in the mornings. On Saturdays, she commutes an hour each way to work and another eight-to-nine hours at a job in her hometown. 

She expressed that the constant work mindset weighs heavy on her shoulders. 

“You have to be there for 47 people emotionally all the time, and you also have to check in with yourself,” A said. “And then I have my other RAs that I have to check in with too.”

Written by Zaynab Masri, Padma Ignatius and Brileigh Guillen
Photo by Reggie Sasaki

Reinstating the SAT is a step backwards for the University of California, and it moves away from its commitment to equitable access, and toward a system that rewards privilege over potential. In July 2026, UC STEM faculty members, from across nine UC campuses, organized a petition to the UC Regents to reinstate SAT and ACT admission requirements after June 2027. The SAT has been marketed as a measure of academic readiness, but more often than not it reflects the resources accessible to a student, rather than their true ability or work ethic. The SAT is inherently biased towards students with more privilege, and the UC system should not be focused on creating more barriers to education, but rather investing in programs that will support existing and future students towards success.

Three drones, so many milestones, and one mission to keep improving! ⚙️

Meet @slugbotics' SOMARS team (Slugs for the Oversight and Management of Aerial Robotic Systems), a #BaskinEngineering-affiliated student team at @ucsc developing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with autonomous flight capabilities. 

What started as a project to build a working drone has evolved into a platform for exploring autonomy, computer vision, and more advanced aerial missions.

The team has developed three quadcopter iterations, each building on lessons from the last:

Iteration 1️⃣: Proved the team could design, build, and successfully fly a functioning UAV.

Iteration 2️⃣: Introduced a custom frame, autonomous flight capabilities, and larger motors and propellers to improve efficiency, with competition in mind.

Iteration 3️⃣: Builds on those improvements, with a target of 45+ minutes of flight time and object detection and payload capabilities.

Now, SOMARS is taking on a new challenge: developing a vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) aircraft that combines the speed and efficiency of fixed-wing flight with a quadcopter’s hovering precision. The project also gives new members an opportunity to learn foundational aerial robotics skills. 

Proud of our #BaskinEngineers for turning every flight into an opportunity to learn and improve! 💛

Image descriptions:
1 - Three students gather around a large quadcopter drone on a table at night.
2 - A student holds a carbon fiber component with a geometric lattice structure.
3 - A student holds a partially assembled drone in Slugworks. The drone has a black frame, exposed wiring, electronic components, and motors.
4 - A student works on the wiring and electronics of a drone frame at a table.
5 - A large quadcopter drone with a yellow upper housing, black arms, and long landing legs stands on a grassy field.
6 - Close-up of a quadcopter drone with a yellow upper housing, illuminated green indicator light, exposed electronics, black frame, and landing legs against a dark background.
7 - Slugbotics team pose together inside @ucscslugworks.

Films, among other forms of art, spark conversations and bring people together. But the platforms and communities that share these pieces of art are just as critical.

This year, the 26th annual Santa Cruz Film Festival (SCFF) featured nine films made by UC Santa Cruz Film and Digital Media (F&DM) undergraduate students and five films made by UCSC alumni. For many UCSC F&DM students, SCFF is an opportunity to share their films and interact with fellow filmmakers and artists.

🤝 Mutual Aid: Providing resources, food, and direct support to students and community members.

💓 EVERY DONATION COUNTS! Whether it’s $1, $5, $10, or $25, no contribution is too small.

Written by the Editorial Board
Illustration by Isu Park

A prevalent trope in the media, constantly reinforced by risk factors like age and social dynamics, is that college campuses are epicenters of sexual assault. But we know it to be true that it’s not just the universities. Sexual assault and the culture that feeds it pervade every level of modern society, from college campuses to the White House. 

While resources for and awareness of sexual assault victims have improved as a product of successful social movements such as #MeToo and sweeping legislation like the Violence Against Women Act, there remains a fatal, glaring gap in accountability culture. 

Read more at the link in our bio.

Support us by donating on Giving Day: 11.18.2026

Giving Day is UCSC’s 24hr fundraising event for community members to join together and support student-run projects and organizations. 

Your support is the backbone of our success. The funds we raise through Giving Day are how we’re able to build our car and compete. Donate now so we can represent UCSC at the annual Formula SAE Electric competition!

Our team is dedicated to designing, engineering, and manufacturing our formula electric race car. We’re a fully student-run organization and we depend on the generosity of sponsors and donors to fulfill our goals. Support us today by donating here or through the link in bio: 
https://give.ucsc.edu/campaigns/82562/donations/new?tc=121792

Every step represents strength, resilience, and hope for those currently fighting, survivors, and the loved ones whose lives have been impacted. As a sisterhood, we are proud to support a cause that brings our community together and reminds us of the importance of unity, compassion, and hope.

Together, we continue to make strides toward a brighter future and a world without breast cancer. 💞

Steps of strength, miles of hope, united as one.🫶🏼🐾

Explore some of our favorite directors and zine publications in our weekly Director/Zine Spotlights! This week we focus on Dreamworldgirl Zine and Jane Schoenbrun. ‧͙⁺˚*･༓☾

Jane Schoenbrun is a transfem, nonbinary filmmaker who aims to depict the horrors of conformity through themes of disembodiment and dysphoria in their films. They are most known for I Saw the TV Glow (2024), Teenage Sex and Death and Camp Miasma (2026), and We’re All Going to the World’s Fair (2021).

Dreamworldgirl Zine is a multimedia publication committed to showcasing writing and art by women and other marginalized gender identities. They publish print and digital issues every summer and winter.

Written by Aayushi Akhani 
Illustration by Mia Moore 

Research funding is the catalyst that made discoveries like vaccines or the Human Genome Project — a map of our genetic makeup curated here at UC Santa Cruz — possible. 

In 2025, the Trump administration slashed roughly $3 billion in scientific research funding by cancelling grants. Renowned establishments such as the National Institute of Health (NIH) and National Science Foundation (NSF) experienced instability as the crackdown on science continued. 

Read at the link in our bio.

💗🎀 Knowledge is power, and awareness saves lives! 🎀💗
The Psi Gamma Chapter of Sigma Lambda Gamma National Sorority, Inc. is bringing awareness to Breast Cancer Awareness Month! From knowing the warning signs to separating myths from facts and sharing helpful resources, early detection and education are so important. 
Remember to check yourself, schedule your screenings, and encourage the women in your life to do the same. You are never alone in this fight! 💕

Think Pink. Spread Awareness. Stand Together. 💗

🎀 Breast Cancer Awareness Resources

1. WomenCARE – Cancer Advocacy, Resources & Education
Website: https://www.womencaresantacruz.org 
2. Breast Cancer Early Detection – Every Woman Counts
Website: https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/every-woman-counts/ 
3. BreastCancer.org
Website: https://www.breastcancer.org

4. Breast & Cervical Cancer Treatment Program (BCCTP)
Website: https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/BCCTP.aspx 
5. Santa Cruz Cancer Benefit Group
Website: https://www.sccbg.org

6. Breast Cancer Financial Assistance
CancerCare: https://www.cancercare.org 
Financial assistance: https://www.cancercare.org/financial 

#PsiGammaChapter #SigmaLambdaGamma #BreastCancerAwareness #EarlyDetectionSavesLives #SLG 💗

🚀 ACM FIELD TRIP: BOXWORKS 2026! 🚀

Want to attend an $850 tech conference for just $20? 👀

Join ACM as we head to BoxWorks 2026 in San Francisco! 💙 Explore the future of AI, technology, and enterprise innovation while hearing from industry leaders like Jensen Huang (CEO of NVIDIA), Lip-Bu Tan (CEO of Intel), and speakers from companies like Anthropic, Samsung, and Cisco!

📅 Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026

📍 Location: San Francisco, CA

⏰ Time: 6:30 AM – 7:00 PM

💸 Registration: $850 conference ticket FULLY COVERED!

🚗 Cost: Just $20/person for gas & parking (transportation provided!)

🎟️ Spots: Only 45 available! Drivers will be prioritized.

🚨 REGISTRATION OPENS FRIDAY, 10/30 AT 12 PM! 🚨

The registration form will be dropped in our ACM Discord, so make sure you’re ready when it goes live!

🔗 Join our Discord through the link in our bio!

✨ Don’t miss this opportunity to network, learn, and experience an exciting tech conference!

Slide 1: Promotional graphic for the UCSC ACM BoxWorks 2026 conference field trip. The design has a white background with light blue decorative corners and dark blue curved accents. Featured speakers include NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, and representatives from Samsung, Anthropic, and Cisco. Event details displayed: Thursday, November 5, San Francisco, 6:30 AM–7 PM. Bottom text reads “swipe to the next slide for more info.”

Slide 2: Informational graphic featuring the ACM logo at the top and a large light blue rounded rectangle containing registration details. Bold text announces that a free-for-all registration form will be released Friday, October 30, at 12 PM. The regular $850 conference registration fee is fully covered. Attendees pay only $20 per person for gas and parking, with transportation provided. Only 45 spots are available, and drivers will be prioritized. Students are instructed to complete the registration form when it is posted in the ACM Discord. The BoxWorks Content + AI logo appears at the bottom.

posts.caption:
On Monday November 2nd please join us in the latest edition of International Palestine Cinema Days. @FilmlabPalestine 

Doors open at 5:30pm at the Resource Center for Nonviolence, please join us in this very special edition of the Visionaries in Action series as we view the film Foragers directed by Jumana Manna. This film depicts the dramas around the practice of foraging for wild edible plants in Palestine with wry humor and a meditative pace. Shot in the Golan Heights, the Galilee and Jerusalem, it employs fiction, documentary and archival footage to portray the impact of Israeli nature protection laws on these customs. 

Please join us in community as we come together to celebrate Palestinian artistry and cinema from 6 - 8:30pm at the Resource Center for Nonviolence. Food will be provided as well! 

#PCDAroundTheWorld
#PCD2026
#FilmlabPalestine 
#FLP

posts.caption:
SISTER ABROAD✈️🌎

Hear from our sister madeleineemiles who’s been studying abroad in Spain! 

“Hi! This fall quarter I am studying abroad in Barcelona, Spain! I came here alone and while it was pretty scary at first I’ve learned to love everything about this experience. I’ve met so many amazing people and traveled to so many beautiful places. Studying abroad has been something I’ve always dreamed about, and it’s been so so awesome so far. My favorite trip so far was going to Dublin and London. The people were so nice and it was so easy to just run into some of the coolest tourist attractions. I only had about 10 hours to explore London, but 30,000 steps and 13 miles later I feel pretty successful. I can’t wait to continue this experience! 😊“

We can’t wait for you to come home Maddie💌

posts.caption:
New Member Monday With poetaylordoc !!!

Meet Poesy! Poesy did Fall 2026 Formal Recruitment and found her home in ucscgammaphibeta !! She has some words of encouragement to share with anyone considering going Panhellenic :)!

Why did you decide to do fall recruitment?

I decided to do fall recruitment to broaden my horizons and meet new people! So far I’ve met the most incredible girls and had so many opportunities to branch out, and I couldn’t be more grateful.

What are you most excited for this year , now that you are in Panhellenic?!

This year I am really looking forward to all of our socials and events, and getting to continue to know all of the girls better!

Any advice for girls considering going Greek that may be nervous?

It’s totally understandable to be nervous going into recruitment, but both the rush process and the outcome are so fun and rewarding, you really have nothing to lose!

posts.caption:
Hey Spatial Squad! 🚁🗺️

The Drone & GIS Society at UCSC is looking for TWO undergraduate officers to help launch Waypoints, a free event series running November 2026 through May 2027. We’re applying for a CITRIS Tech for Social Good grant to fund it, and we need two undergrads on the team to submit, so we’re moving fast!

No drone or GIS experience needed. Any major, any undergrad year. If you’re curious, organized, or just like bringing people together, we want to hear from you!

📩 Apply by 10/31/2026: email dgsscucsc@gmail.com with your name, UCSC email, major, year, the role you want (or both), and why you’re interested. Any relevant experience is a bonus but totally optional.

Questions? Email us at dgsscucsc@gmail.com and the whole team (Max Tcheng, Denise Marc, and Dr. Bo Yang) will see it.

Not ready to lead? Join our Google Group, check out our website (link in bio), and follow @dgssc_ucsc and @ucsc_gistar. More committee roles are coming soon, so let us know if you’d like to help in a different way. Share with your networks!

Stay fly,
The Drone & GIS Society Team

Photographs of the agents can be found on YARR’s Facebook and Instagram (yarr.scc). 

Fotografías tomadas de los agentes se pueden ver en las páginas de Facebook e Instagram de la YARR.

posts.caption:
Written by Ava Smith and Melissa Pilato
Photos by Priscilla Liu

“This incredible little butterfly that weighs the same as a paperclip [is] migrating hundreds to thousands of miles each direction and surviving the winter,” said Isis Howard, a conservation biologist working on the endangered species team at the Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation.

Santa Cruz’s Natural Bridges State Park is ranked among the top 10 western monarch overwintering sites in California — a sheltered grove where monarchs cluster to conserve energy and keep warm in the winter. Monarch butterflies, scientifically known as Danaus plexippus, soar through the sky, dancing in circles around each other and hanging like leaves from the branches of the coastal eucalyptus trees in the grove.

Written by Aayushi Akhani and Ashley Palma-Jimenez
Photos by Reggie Sasaki

Isa Santos is a first-year astrophysics major at UC Santa Cruz with an 8 a.m. class every Thursday. Ideally, Santos would get dressed, grab breakfast at the nearest dining hall and travel to her class.

But due to the reduced dining hall hours implemented earlier this year, she often misses out on the nutrition she needs at breakfast time.

“Instead of being able to eat first thing before class, I have to skip breakfast in order to make it to my early morning classes,” Santos said. “I also have to check which dining halls are open because Crown/Merrill is closed during weekends, which can interrupt my studying time.”

Written by Lila Toledo and Liv Palaz
Photos by Isla Patrick

UC Santa Cruz affiliates make up approximately 80 percent of BCycle ridership in Santa Cruz County. However, the service is coming to a swift end for on-campus bikers. 

This past September, UCSC Public Affairs sent an email to students and staff announcing that BCycle is canceling their contract with the university earlier than anticipated. Though a specific removal date was not announced in the email, in a statement to City on a Hill Press, BCycle Santa Cruz clarified the removal is expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

posts.caption: Hi everyone! My name is Emma and I’m a Biomolecular Engineering graduate. I joined iGEM because of the independence, collaboration, and critical thinking that it involves. It has been so amazing to work with this group over the past 10 months. From interviews, to brainstorming sessions, late nights in lab, and having results that we are proud to present. It has taught me to push myself to think outside of the box as an engineer, and to be a better leader. I’m looking for a role in Research and Development, and have a passion for cancer research. When I’m not in lab, I enjoy going to the beach, hiking, running, exploring new places whether nearby or across the world, and spending time with my friends and family.

posts.caption:
October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and the sisters of Sigma Omicron Pi want to bring awareness to highlight a critical health issue of the rising rates of breast cancer among Asian American women. Understanding our bodies and knowing what to look out for is one of the most crucial steps we can take for our health.

Remember! Experiencing one or more of these symptoms does not automatically mean you have breast cancer. Many of these signs can be linked to non-cancerous conditions such as cysts, hormonal changes, or infections.

However, if you notice any changes in your body, please schedule an appointment with a doctor or healthcare provider right away so you can get a professional evaluation.

Source: https://cancer.ucsf.edu/news/2026/07/13/ucsf-study-breast-cancer-is-rising-fast-in-asian-american-women

https://www.bcrf.org/about-breast-cancer/asian-women-aapi-women-breast-cancer/?campaign=840664

https://breastcancernow.org/about-breast-cancer/awareness/signs-and-symptoms-of-breast-cancer

posts.caption:
Written by Bryce Chen and Isabel White
Photos by Reggie Sasaki and Keith Gelderloos

Two fires ignited today on the west side of UC Santa Cruz’s main campus at about 3:45 p.m. Both fires are now extinguished. One fire began in the forested area between the Academic Resource Center (ARC) and McHenry Library. The other began in a forested area near Porter Meadow, close to Parking Lot 125. 

City on a Hill Press reporters were unable to speak to Santa Cruz fire marshals who were managing the scene. According to several police officers on scene, the cause of the fires has not been determined yet. However, officers alluded that an individual may have started the fires. 

“We were very fortunate that there was no wind today, so the fires were able to be put out fairly quickly,” said Steve Walpole, the captain of the UCSC Police Department. “If this was a high wind day, this could have been a much more serious incident.”

This story will be posted on our website in the next few hours. Read more at the link in our bio.

I joined iGEM for a second time this year to continue building my research skills and contribute to an incredible team where I could help shape a project from the ground up.

I’ve loved working alongside such a creative and passionate group of people! Through this experience, we’ve learned to approach challenges with perseverance and resourcefulness, allowing for me to grow a lot both as a researcher and as a person.

After graduation, I hope to pursue a career focused on developing alternative therapeutics and making critical healthcare more accessible to underserved communities.

When I’m not in the lab, you can usually find me outdoors, whether that’s backpacking, biking, hiking, or exploring somewhere new!

“Hii my name is Maddie Hoang and I’m a senior  from Berkeley, CA majoring in Neuroscience and Psychology. I joined Kappa Fall 2023 and it has made such an amazing impact on my life here in Santa Cruz. Looking back I didn’t know what to expect going into recruitment , but I have now met so amazing girls that I can proudly call sisters and I’m so grateful that I’m able to spend everyday with them. They’ve been by my side through many ups and downs the past few year and I wouldn’t be here without them. Not only has Kappa given me a sisterhood, but also strength, drive, and passion. I’ve had the opportunity to serve an Events Director and Now VP of External Affairs and have had so much fun working with all my directors and chapter to make Kappa so special. I can’t wait to spend this last year with these ladies and make even more memories with them💙🦋”

posts.caption:
Somebody in Panhellenic loves you 🩷

#panhellenic#sorority#gogreek

Saniya + Ava,

I’m forever grateful that panhellenic brought us together.

You are both such amazing, intelligent, and kind women that inspire me constantly. Saniya, you never fail to make me smile and I love that you’re willing to speak out for your friends. #10toesdown Ava, your warmth always lifts my mood and you are the best problem solver/decision maker in tough situations. Thank you for giving me the chance to open up and gain two incredible friendships.

To many more hangouts with us and love, olivia.

much love, 
Isabel

Dear Lola, 

When I met you during recruitment I knew you would become an important person in my life. I’m so grateful to have you as my big and I’m forever thankful for your wisdom, loyalty, and empathy. I have learned so much from you and I know that will continue. You understand me like no one else and I know you always have my back. 

Love, Ella

Dear Jackie and Bryanna, 

I will forever be grateful to GPhi for bringing me to you both. I can’t remember exactly how we met or when we became so close, but regardless, our friendship is one of the things I cherish most about my time at UCSC. You two genuinely make my life so much brighter, and I know that no matter what, you’ll always be there for me. From our San Jose In-N-Out runs to our random inside jokes that almost cause us to crash our cars, you both bring so much joy and laughter into my life. You inspire me every day to find happiness in the little things, smile a little more, and see the good in everything. I feel so lucky to have you both in my life, and I honestly can’t imagine my college experience without you. I love you guys so much more than you know and I can’t wait to make more memories with you. 

Madison

Ava,
Ava was the first friend I met here at UCSC. We have so many memories together and we are even roommates this year! We went through recruitment together, and even though we ended up in different organizations, my love for her is inexplicable. All of our late night debriefs, walks on the track, spa nights, gym days, study sessions, and sleepovers are things I will cherish forever. She is my numbe

I have spent the summer asking questions, being comfortable with uncertainty, and working through challenges together as a team. posts.caption:
Written by Alessandra Ashford and Melissa Pilato 
Illustration by Isabel Louie

“As an international student coming to the U.S. on an exchange, it’s everything you’re asking for,”  said “S,” a former UCDC participant from France who wishes to remain anonymous. “To visit everything and to see everything — I think that it’s two very different experiences — and [this is] a chance to be able to do that.”

Programs like the University of California Washington Program (UCDC) have allowed international students at UCSC to gain academic credit while being a part of an immersive internship.

“You [can] have an experience in California and a completely other one on the East Coast, and [UCDC] can teach you more about the U.S.,” she continued.

But due to recent threats from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), these programs could all change for international students.

Read more at the link in our bio

posts.caption:
Key friendship friday 🗝️💙 Here’s messages Audrey and Addie have for each other!

“Dear Addie,
I am so lucky I met you through Kappa. You are so kind and always know how to make me laugh. Thank you for always being there for me whether it’s me ranting or debriefing and always knowing how to put a smile on my face. I know if I am having a bad day I can talk to you and feel so much better. I love all of our spontaneous side quests we go on and random situations we get in. You make even the ordinary days so much more fun, and I wouldn’t trade our memories for anything. I am so happy we are roommates this year and I love that I get to hang out with you every day. You have become so much more than just a friend to me, you are my ride or die and I can’t wait for this year.
Love you so much!
Audrey”
•
•
•
“Dear Audrey,
I’m so grateful that Kappa brought you into my life and I now get to be roommates with you!! 
You are one of the kindest, genuine, and funny people I have ever met. You are an inspiration and have changed my life in more ways than you know. Thank you for always being there for me and listening to all my rants. I love our movie couch nights and how all of our roommates fall asleep mid movie. 
Most of all I love that no matter what we are doing I will always be laughing and having the best time ever. We literally do anything and everything together and I wouldn’t change it for the world!! 
Love, Addie 🩷“

#ucsckappa #kappakappagamma #keyfriendshipfriday

We hope that you can join us for some gardening this Sunday morning at the Homeless Garden Project farm located near natural bridges. We will be there from 10 a.m.- 12:00 p.m. The Homeless Garden Project hosts drop-in volunteer hours on weekends from 10am - 4pm. Here are some reminders and more information:

    •    Please bring your own lunch/snacks and plenty of  water
    •    If it’s raining, the volunteer workday will be canceled
    •    Please do not come to the farm if you are feeling sick or are experiencing any COVID-19 symptoms
    •    Volunteers must wear a mask inside farm buildings, within 6 feet of others, and in the lunch line, regardless of vaccination status

Meet the one and only Rtr. Mohamed Murshid Akram Jiffry Bawa, “Bawa” or our Rota Presi Ayya! 🤍✨

Soft-spoken, kind, and deeply respectful, he always leads with quiet warmth. But behind that calm exterior lies effortless confidence, pure charisma, and just enough chaos to keep the club laughing.

Confidence overloader? 100%! He’ll hype you up, then roast you when you least expect it! 😂
That “girl-catching” smile? Absolutely iconic! 😭😂
Always on time? Let's just say… we’re still waiting! 😭
Matale memories? Two mountain jumps, one legendary WhatsApp sticker! 💀

Our Immediate Past President for RI Year 2026/27. Once our Presi, forever our favourite Presi Ayya! 🫡🤍

On October 3rd, 2026, Kappa Zeta Sorority celebrated 23 wonderful years at UC Santa Cruz

Kappa Zeta was founded on October 3, 2003 at the University of California, Santa Cruz. Kappa Zeta quickly became known for its multicultural membership, dedication to philanthropy for women and children, and commitment to academic excellence. 

We honor and thank our 13 founding sisters for creating a welcoming, supportive, and empowering space that has continued to thrive since 2003, and will carry on for many more years to come. 

Happy 23rd Founders Day, Kappa Zeta!

posts.caption:
‼️📢 INTEL FIELD TRIP 📢 ‼️ 

ACM and SASE are partnering for a company field trip to Intel’s HQ in Santa Clara on Friday, 10/16 from 12PM-4PM! It’ll be a collaboration event with clubs from SJSU.

We have 25 slots available. A form will be released on Friday, 10/9, at 2PM in the ACM and SASE Discords. Discord links are in the respective club profiles. The form will be first come first serve. Drivers will be prioritized. 

Swipe to view more information regarding the event! We hope to see you there.

Alt text:

First slide: Graphic advertising company field trip to Intel. There are 25 slots available and there will be a first come first serve form sent in club Discords. Drivers will be prioritized. 

Second slide: Slide includes event information. The event will have 7-10 Intel mentors/panelists from engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and other fields.
The schedule is:
• 12:00PM: Leave campus
• 1:00 PM: Arrive at Intel
• 1:15 PM: Hard cutoff for entry
• 1:20-2:50 PM: Q&A panel
• 2:50-3:50 PM: Networking
• 3:50-4:00 PM: Raffle
There will also be a lot of giveaways, including 20 barebone systems, an i7 gaming laptop, 3 desktop PCs, and Intel swag. Everyone gets raffle tickets at entry and can earn more by asking questions and networking.
People who can drive will be prioritized!

posts.caption:
FogNet is a research, innovation, and commercialization effort focused on improving fog water harvesting for drinking water and irrigation, and on analyzing fog water’s chemical composition. Students can contribute to three main project areas: fog nets for irrigation water, fog harps for water quality and drinking water, and active collectors for atmospheric chemistry research. The team is looking for a wide range of skill sets, including market research, business development, manufacturing optimization, mechanical engineering, CAD, circuits and electrical engineering, data analysis, outreach, and promotion.

Join us on October 7, from 1–2 p.m. in our Classroom Space (BE‑97) to explore these questions and learn how to get involved. You’ll have the opportunity to meet Dr. Weiss‑Penzias and discover how fog harvesting, an inventive blend of science and innovation, can generate powerful solutions to unconventional environmental challenges and how to get involved in the project yourself!

📸 Image description:

A photo of Dr. Peter Weiss and FogSquad undergraduate students, standing in a field showing off their FogNet prototype with a stylized text header which reads “What’s the deal with Fogsquad?”. The subtitle reads “Wednesday, October 7 / BE-97 / 1:00 - 2:00 PM”

#GetInvolved #FogSquad #StudentWorkOpportunity #UCSCSlugworks #CreatorSpace

posts.caption:
🍂 Hola Cafecitxs! 🍂

Meet the 2026-2027 C.A.F.E. board! 🤎We’re so excited to introduce our new and returning members for the school year! 📚🦌

Get to know us a little more by scrolling and finding out some fun facts about each board member! ☺️🧑‍💻

Dulce is our founder and president of C.A.F.E. ☕️ Her hometown is Los Angeles and fourth year triple major in Psychology, Latin American and Latino Studies/ Education, Justice, Democracy. 😮‍💨 

Dulce is Guatemalan, Salvadoran, & Honduran and an activity she loves to do with her family is to decorate the Christmas tree and house a certain color while wearing matching PJs to match the theme 🎄⛄️

David is our vice president of C.A.F.E. ☕️ His hometown is Los Angeles and a third year double major in Neuroscience and Education. 🧠 ✏️ 

David is Salvadoran and a favorite tradition of his is to visit El Salvador during Christmas!🇸🇻🎅

Rocío is our secretary of C.A.F.E.☕️ Her hometown is Sacramento and a fourth year double major in Psychology and Latin American & Latino Studies. 👤🌎

Rocío is Guatemalan and a family tradition she loves to do is bake traditional bread for Semana Santa in March!🥖🌷

Kate is our publicity chair of C.A.F.E. ☕️ Her hometown is Long Beach and a fourth year double major in Psychology and Sociology. 🫂👩🏻‍💻

Kate is Salvadoran and Guatemalan and a favorite activity she loves to do is to cook pupusas with her mom when she goes home from school! 🫓😋

posts.caption:
SANTA CRUZ DEVFEST 🚀 NOV 14-15

We’re excited to introduce GDG DevFest Santa Cruz, a technology-focused event bringing together students, developers, and tech enthusiasts for a day of learning, building, and connecting with the broader tech community.

DevFest is an opportunity to explore emerging technologies, learn from industry professionals, work on hands-on projects, and connect with other students who are interested in technology. All experience levels are welcome, whether you’re an experienced developer or just beginning your journey in tech.

📅 DevFest: November 14/15
⭐ Priority Applications: October 2–11
📝 Regular Applications: October 12–28
📬 Application Decisions: November 2

Priority applications are officially open, so submit yours before October 11 for priority consideration.

🔗 Apply at ucsc-devfest.com 

We can’t wait to see what you build! 💻

#GDG #GDGDevFest #DevFest2026 #UCSC #GoogleDevelopers

Slide 1 - A light gray graphic featuring a large black “DevFest” title framed by yellow brackets, “Santa Cruz” below, GDG branding and colorful decorative elements in the center, and “November 14th to 15th” at the bottom.
Slide 2 - A pale yellow graphic titled “What is DevFest,” with GDG branding in the upper right and a large white text box describing DevFest, its 2026 theme, and its focus on AI, developer tools, and emerging technologies.
Slide 3 - A dark graphic featuring a vertical timeline with colored markers for application deadlines, decision release, and the November 14–15 DevFest event, plus an “Apply now” callout and website on the right.
Slide 4 - A light gray graphic titled “What to Expect at DevFest,” featuring three large colored panels highlighting $2,000 in prizes, industry speakers, and project judges.
Slide 5 - A red-orange graphic with “Apply Today” at the top, GDG branding and decorative graphics, and a large yellow text box encouraging students of all experience levels to build, connect, network, and explore professional opportunities.

As always, we wish to make all on-campus events accessible. For accommodations please contact SOAR at soar@ucsc.edu!

Keep in mind, to receive an invitation to our final Closed Recruitment Invite Only Event, you must:
• Attend 2+ Open Recruitment events
• Have a 2.8+ GPA
• Submit a completed Recruitment Application prior to the announced deadline
• Actively pursue the following eligible majors/minors: All those under the Baskin School of Engineering, as well as Business Management Economics, Economics, and Global Economics

You can also request a ride by filling out this: https://forms.gle/VJVr1ujz15byVeK57

Keep in mind, to receive an invitation to our final Closed Recruitment Invite Only Event, you must:
• Attend 2+ Open Recruitment events
• Have a 2.8+ GPA
• Submit a completed Recruitment Application prior to the announced deadline
• Actively pursue the following eligible majors/minors: All those under the Baskin School of Engineering, as well as Business Management Economics, Economics, and Global Economics

posts.caption:
BELLOO HERMANESS!! 

Tell your friend to tell a friend that we’re backkk🙈‼️ We hope you all had a lit and relaxing summer. As summer classes are starting up again, we want to have that summer vibezzzz 🌅🌞 hangout to ease us back into the new school year 📝. Whether you’ve joined us before or not, we’d love to see new and returning members having a blast 💥. Join us at our first social of the year! Enjoy mini card games, bingo, and s’mores with us 🔥🪵! 

📆: October 2nd 
📍: Seabright Beach
⏰: 7-9PM 

If you are unsure of how to get to Seabright Beach, no worries! 🙈
• Meet up at the Quarry before 6:20PM ⏰‼️ (Steering Members will be there to guide you to Seabright)
• Get off the 19 bus at the Pacific Ave/ Front (Wharf) Bus Stop 🚏🛑
• Walk all of the Boardwalk on the outer side until you reach a ramp 🎢 🤘🏼
• Walk up the ramp and across the bridge next to the train tracks 🌉 🚂 🛤️
• Walk up another ramp and make a sharp right ➡️
• Follow the sidewalk until you reach the Seabright Beach sign! 🪧 
• Download the transit app if you are unsure and/or can't meet up with Steering before 6:20PM! 🚍📲

🚪OPEN DOOR POLICY🚪Anyone and everyone ‼️ is welcome to join us whether you’ve been here before or are new 🙂‍↕️🙂‍↕️ and want to check us out! Pull up anytime ⏰, even if you think it’s too late to pull up because it’s neverrrr too late 🙅🏽‍♀️🙅🏽‍♂️❌! 

We hope to see you there! 🩷🤍🤎

posts.caption:
The first event of Fall 2026 Recruitment is here. 

The Pi Chi Chapter of Delta Sigma Pi formally invites you to Start Your Legacy with our Meet The Chapter Event: September 28th at 6:00 PM in the Redwood Lounge. The attire is Business Casual. 

As always, we wish to make all on-campus events accessible. For accommodations contact soar@ucsc.edu.

Keep in mind, to receive an invitation to our final Closed Recruitment Invite Only Event, you must:
• Attend 2+ Open Recruitment events
• Have a 2.8+ GPA

BUILT TO SERVE 🌎
What does it mean to serve? It’s more than a title or an award; it’s showing up with intention, leading with compassion, and making a difference in the communities around us. 🫶
We’re glad to honor Sara Hernandez and Sofia Perez as our 25–26 Built to Serve recipients! 🎉 Their dedication to service through MEDLIFE, their SLT experiences, and their commitment to health equity and community empowerment embody what it truly means to serve.
From Ecuador and Cusco to Costa Rica and Lima, their journeys remind us that meaningful change can start with one opportunity, one community, and one person willing to show up. 🤝
Congratulations, Sara & Sofia! We’re so glad to be sharing your story. We will forever be grateful for the impact you’ve made and excited to see where your commitment to service takes you next. ❤️💛
Built to Serve. Built to make a difference. 
#ucsc#medlife#impact#change#bethechange

The latest MATE competition wraps up and makes way for the upcoming school year. Slugbotics in an engineering club that welcomes all grades and experience levels. 
Our club is supporting five projects this year:

✶ MATE — An underwater robotics team building a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV).
✶ SOMARS — The resident drone and aerial robotics team.
✶ Combat Robotics — It’s in the name. Builds battle robots that beat up other bots.
✶ Rover — Builds Mars and Lunar rovers and competes with them.
✶ Car Team — The self-driving autonomous RC car team.

Discord is the main medium of communication for all project teams. You can find the link to join in our bio. Joining this server is the first step to being an active member of this club. This is where we post all of our club-wide announcements, and also where you can communicate with each individual project team and its leads.

posts.caption:
Meet Our Recruitment Unit: 
Here’s some words from our wonderful Philanthropy director Lili! 

Hi everyone! My name is Lili and I’m an incoming third-year majoring in politics and legal studies. Being a part of PAD has given me the ability to explore the legal field beyond the classroom while expanding my knowledge, pursuing my interests, and developing a clearer vision of what my future in law may look like.
Aside from that, I’ve also really valued the opportunity to connect with people who share similar goals and interests while also bringing their own unique approaches to the legal field. As Philanthropy Chair, I’ve enjoyed finding meaningful ways to give back to the community and creating experiences for our PAD members to make a positive impact. This role has also helped me grow personally and gain a deeper appreciation for volunteering and community  involvement. I’m especially looking forward to meeting new recruits this fall and supporting them as they embark on their new journey with PAD! 💛💜🤞🏼

Meet Our Recruitment Unit: 
Here’s some words from our wonderful Secretary Layla Cortes! 

Hey everyone! I’m Layla Cortes, an incoming 2nd year majoring in Legal studies and secretary of Phi Alpha Delta. My first year and quarter at UCSC is when I joined PAD hoping to find a community with students that were also interested in the law field. Not only did I find a community but Phi Alpha Delta has given me so many opportunities and experiences to interact with law experts and expose myself to different law paths. PAD has given me time to truly find the type of law I want to pursue and interact with others so I may support them the same way. As a board member, I am truly grateful for the executive board and I hope to engage with other students who want to explore the huge field of law. Can’t wait for this year and to see more people join PAD! ⚖️👩🏽‍⚖️💜

posts.caption:
🎉Hola Familia🎉

Today, we celebrate Central American Independence day. The act of independence was signed in Guatemala City which declared the freedom of El Salvador, Honduras, Costa Rica, Guatemala, and Nicaragua👏. We celebrate it by honoring our past, celebrating our culture, and living our history❤️. We are proud to be Central American and we are excited to be celebrating this independence day with you all!🇬🇹🇭🇳🇳🇮🇨🇷🇸🇻

Here are some popular dishes of the countries represented today!😋

Pupusas are a popular dish from El Salvador, which is stuffed with many different fillings you want and with a masa base. They also are topped with red salsa and a vinegar cabbage slaw called curitdo🫓🇸🇻.

Baleda is a traditional Honduran food that is made with a thick flour tortilla that is usually filled with mashed beans, fresh cream, and queso duro🫘🇭🇳.

Gallo pinto is the national dish of Costa Rica which is usually white rice and beans fried together. The name translates from Spanish as the “spotted rooster” 🐓 🇨🇷.

Guatemalan Tamales stand out from other tamales because of their use of plantain leaves instead of corn husks and the masa being more fluffy and soft instead of a little bit harder than most tamales 🫒🇬🇹.

Vigorón is a traditional food from Nicaragua that is served on a plantain leaf and topped with yuca, chicharrones, and curtido. Traditionally, it is eaten with your hands instead of utensils 🍴 🇳🇮.

We collaborate with companies for company visits (such as Pinterest), fully-fund students to attend conferences (such as the Grace Hopper Conference), and host events such as technical workshops and social networking events.

All officers are expected to attend the weekly officer meetings.

We are currently recruiting for:
- Secretary
- Treasurer
- Instruction Lead
- Social Media Chair

If you’re interested in becoming an officer for our club, please fill out the application through the QR code or link in our bio!

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. You may apply to as many officer positions as you’d like.

posts.caption:
Our members have been busy this summer! IBA members spent their summer gaining hands-on experience across a wide range of companies, roles, and industries. Each experience brings new skills, perspectives, and knowledge to the table. Take a look at what they worked on, what they learned, and what they’re bringing back to IBA this fall!

This summer, I interned with KPMG’s State & Local Tax practice, supporting asset management clients across tax compliance and advisory engagements. My work included preparing tax workpapers and roll-forwards, conducting XML audits and data analysis in Excel, and communicating with clients to gather and reconcile financial information. I also contributed to an intern research project analyzing California SB 122 and built tax models to help companies evaluate opportunities to strategically utilize tax credits and reduce their tax liabilities. Through the internship, I strengthened my Excel, tax, and financial analysis skills while learning how to communicate effectively with clients and approach complex problems in a professional services environment.

During my internship at Gilead, I looked at procurement spend data to identify key trends and built an AI agent that can access and analyze that data to support daily decision making. I also conducted industry benchmarking and research around data analytics, KPIs, and emerging technologies, helping turn those findings into strategic recommendations. Overall, I gained experience using financial data and analytics to support more informed business decisions.

Over this past summer, I spent 3 months in Berlin, Germany, working at Le Magasin. I built multiple investor-facing cash flow and P/L models for our upcoming activations in North America. I also found a limitation in their business model that led me to model out our entire purchasing strategy, where I identified a 350% blended margin upside. Lastly, I created countless budgets going along with our current activations in the EU.

🎓CAFE GRADUATE SPOTLIGHT:GIO 🎓

Today, we’re celebrating someone who holds a special place in the C.A.F.E. familia — Gio, our former Publicity Chair. 💚

Gio, thank you for everything you poured into C.A.F.E. From the creativity you brought to our publicity to the time, energy, and heart you gave to our comunidad, your presence made a difference. 🫶🏽

You helped make sure C.A.F.E. was not only seen, but that our stories, cultures, and voices were seen too. 🌎✨ And while your title may have been Publicity Chair, your impact went far beyond that.
One of the most beautiful things about C.A.F.E. is watching our members grow, graduate, and take everything they’ve learned and experienced with them into their next chapter. We hope you know that a piece of your work, your creativity, and your corazón will always remain part of the comunidad you helped build☕️💚

We’re so incredibly proud of you, Gio. 🎓🥹 As you close this chapter and step into whatever comes next, we hope you remember how far you’ve come and how many people you’ve inspired along the way.
Thank you for being part of our story. Thank you for helping build C.A.F.E. And thank you for being you. 💚
Congratulations, Gio! 🎓✨

Once a Cafecitx, always a Cafecitx. ☕️🌎💚

Con mucho cariño,
Your C.A.F.E. Familia 🫶🏽

Today, we celebrate the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan’s independence. In October 1990, the Supreme Council changed the country’s name to the Kyrgyz Republic, and on December 15, the Declaration of State Sovereignty was adopted. Then, on August 31, 1991, Kyrgyzstan officially declared its independence.
Independence gave the Kyrgyz people the opportunity to shape our own future, preserve our culture and traditions, and build our nation as a sovereign state.🇰🇬

posts.caption:
Some moments from SOMARS in the Mojave 🏜️🏜️🏜️

SOMARS (Slugs for the Oversight and Management of Aerial Robotics Systems) aka Drone team recently competed at the California Unmanned Aerial Systems Competition earlier this summer.

However, before competition they spent the entire school year developing their autonomous drone: “Calligula”

The team faced the typical challenges of 

1. A machine breaking for demo day, resulting in fun all hours fixing the problem
2. Forgetting the drones Remote ID and ordering a new one from the Airbnb
3. Needing to purchase a Lowe’s fan for printing with nylon-CF, 
4. And more!

But the successes were amazing!

Autonomous flight over 150 ft AGL in 30+ mph gusts of wind proved the tuning of the drone and the camera systems were able to give us amazing FPV footage. 

@mccormick.exe piloted the drone which resulted in Slugbotics to be the ONLY team to complete the bucket retrieval mission!!!

We are looking forward to the upcoming SUAS competition in Oklahoma and meeting new members that want to learn more in the fall!

Lastly, we want to thank @baskinengineering for all their support.

As always, Discord LINK IN BIO 👾

posts.caption:
Hello Cosplay Club!! Long time no see!

Hoping you are all doing well this summer! As we approach our fall quarter, I’d like to make a big announcement!

Cosplay Club is currently recruiting officers! 

We currently have vacancies in the positions of secretary and PR! 

Our process to recruit officers goes as follows: if you are interested, respond to the **attached form below**. From there, we will schedule interviews with applicants (they will be casual, no need to stress over them!) and then decide between the officers who we think is the best fit!

Requirements:
In order to interview for an officer position, you must be a member for at least one whole quarter prior to interviewing. Meaning, If you are a brand new member, you cannot apply at this time. 
Other requirements
- Must be a currently registered student at UCSC
- Must be able to participate in 80% of the meetings per quarter unless a valid excuse is given
- Must be able to frequently attend and/or help prepare for events
- Must be able to attend officer meetings (times and dates of meetings will be scheduled together by the officers ahead of time)
- Must be able to provide timely responses to urgent club communication
- Must be in good standing with Slugworks

If you have any questions about these requirements or would like any clarification, please message us! 

Applications will close September 4th, so make sure to submit before then! 
Please message us if you have any questions at all, and we hope to see you apply!

https://forms.gle/W5LDFUFmS2k767Vj8

posts.caption:
To our friends, the greater Santa Cruz Community, and brothers nationwide, it is with great sadness and heavy hearts that we share the news of the passing of our Beloved Chapter Brother, #56 Kirin “Eshu” Rajagopalan. 

Kirin’s sudden passing has been really difficult for all of us – Kirin was such an integral part of the bonds we formed during our undergraduate careers, the bonds we maintained in our adult lives post-graduation, and the bonds we continued to foster with our incoming brothers. 

His presence, light, laughter, kindness, and wisdom were and will continue to be at the core of the memories we cherish. As well as the qualities we will continue to embody. 

His family raised and helped shape such a wonderful man: he made everyone feel welcome, as if they belonged and were part of something bigger. As he would say, we’re a motley crew of random dudes – but it works, and we always got each other’s backs and our communities.

If you find yourself so inclined to donate to his Memory and Honor, as well as assist the Rajagopalan family with the unexpected expenses of laying their precious child to rest. Please donate to the chapter on Venmo with the comment “Rest in Power, ESHU”. 

https://account.venmo.com/u/SantaCruzBetas 

In advance, thank you for loving and supporting our brother and his family. 

-Much Love, Lethal Lambda Gamma.

Looking for a way to make a difference, meet new people, and get involved on campus? We’d love to have you on our team!

As a member of Enviroslug, you’ll have the opportunity to:
🌎 Organize events like Earth Summit
🤝 Build lasting friendships and community
🎪 Table at campus events and connect with students
💡 Share your ideas and develop leadership skills
✈️ Attend sustainability conferences and represent UCSC
🌿 Create positive environmental change on campus
✨ Open to all majors and all years! No previous experience is required, just a passion for learning, community, and the environment.

Interested in joining? Email us at envirosl@ucsc.edu to learn more!

#Enviroslug #UCSC #Sustainability #EnvironmentalJustice #StudentLeadership

Image Description: A collage of Enviroslug members participating in activities throughout the year, including team-building, tabling on campus, organizing Earth Summit, collaborating in meetings, attending a sustainability conference, and hosting community events. The images highlight opportunities to build friendships, develop leadership skills, and create positive environmental change at UC Santa Cruz.
