Thank you for the years of dedication, leadership, and care you have poured into this space. You organized, advocated, educated, and showed up time and time again in service of sustainability, environmental justice, and a better future.

Your impact will be felt long after graduation through the communities you strengthened and the people you inspired. We are endlessly grateful for all that you have contributed to Enviroslug.

As you begin your next chapter, we know you will continue creating positive change wherever you go. No matter where life takes you, Enviroslug will always be your home.

Congratulations, graduates! We can’t wait to see all the amazing things you’ll accomplish. 💚 ✨

posts.caption:
That's a wrap on another incredible year with ESLP! 

This year was filled with meaningful conversations, inspiring guest speakers, hands-on learning, community events, environmental action, retreats, and so many unforgettable memories. Together, we built community, explored environmental justice, challenged ourselves to think critically, and supported one another every step of the way.

To everyone who attended our events, enrolled in CRSN 61, collaborated with us, and helped create these experiences, thank you. And to our graduating members, thank you for everything you've contributed to our community. We can't wait to see where your journeys take you next.

Peace out and have an amazing summer <3

Image Description: This carousel celebrates the Education for Sustainable Living Program's (ESLP) year in review at UC Santa Cruz. The post highlights a year of environmental education, community organizing, leadership development, and student engagement through photos from workshops, discussion events, guest speakers, campus programs, outdoor activities, advocacy campaigns, class sessions, retreats, and end-of-year celebrations. Throughout the carousel, students collaborate on creative projects, participate in environmental justice discussions, organize campus events, connect with guest speakers, build community outdoors, and celebrate graduating members. The overall design uses scrapbook-inspired graphics with pastel colors, hand-drawn illustrations, flowers, and cut-out lettering to reflect a year of learning, friendship, and collective action.

✨ ISA Board Applications for 2026–2027 are now open! ✨
We’re incredibly excited for the year ahead filled with new ideas, events, and all the memories that come with them. Joining ISA Board is a chance to have a genuine impact on the campus community while working with a group of people who care about creating meaningful experiences for others. It’s also one of the best ways to meet new people and form friendships that last far beyond a single school year.
ISA is open to everyone, regardless of background. 

While we love celebrating South Asian culture, our community has always been about bringing people together, learning from one another, and creating a space where everyone feels welcome. If you’ve ever attended an ISA event and thought, “I’d love to help make something like this happen,” this is your opportunity to do exactly that.

We’d love to see your application and hear the ideas you want to bring to life!! Show us how creative you can get:)🤍💚🧡

Congratulations to the members that participated, we are so proud of you!👏

💛Take a moment for yourself this quarter. 💛

Join ChALE for a Mental Health Workshop with UCSC alumna and Clinical Counselor Laurene Dominguez as we explore healing, wellness, cultural identity, community support, and strategies for maintaining balance in our everyday lives.

🗓 Tuesday, June 9th
⏰ 1:15 PM – 4:45 PM
📍 Redwood Lounge
🍽 Food Provided

Together, we’ll discuss:
✨ Mental health and self-care
✨ Limpias
✨ Chicanx/Latinx community support
✨ Healthy relationships and anxiety
✨ Social justice and wellness
✨ Indigenous and Western healing practices
✨ Cultural identity and belonging

Whether you’re looking to learn new tools, connect with community, or simply take a break and invest in your well-being, this space is for you. 💛

You belong here. You are not alone. Your mental health matters.
🔗 RSVP through the QR code on the flyer!

This past Tuesday, we had the honor of welcoming Chris Yeh to campus. Chris brought an inspiring perspective from his experience in venture capital, entrepreneurship, and blitzscaling, while emphasizing the importance of staying grounded, curious, and resilient throughout your career. He also shared meaningful insights from his personal journey in figuring out the meaning and purpose of life, which added a deeper and more thoughtful perspective to the conversation.

We’re especially grateful for the personal stories and insights he shared from his own journey, which made the conversation even more impactful and genuine. Thank you as well to Chris for bringing a copy of his book “Blitzscaling: The Lightning-Fast Path to Building Massively Valuable Companies” to give away to one of our members!

Thank you to everyone who attended and engaged in such an impactful conversation, and a special thank you to members clydecollado and kylerachien for leading the discussion!

posts.caption:
🏆 KAMPITITION 2026 IS TODAY! 🌊

Last but not least, we’re closing out our Filipino mythology countdown with the Sirena and the Bungisngis. 🇵🇭✨

The Sirena, known as the mermaid of Filipino folklore, is a mysterious sea being often associated with beauty, enchantment, and the power of the ocean. 🌊🧜‍♀️ Meanwhile, the Bungisngis is a one-eyed giant famous for its booming laughter and playful yet intimidating presence. 👁️ Despite its fearsome appearance, the Bungisngis is remembered for its humor and larger-than-life personality.

From the depths of the sea to echoing laughter in the mountains, these legends remind us of the imagination and storytelling woven throughout Filipino culture.

KAMPERS, we can’t wait to see you all TODAY at KAMPITITION 2026! 💪⚡

☀️ It’s going to be HOT, so please come prepared! Bring:
💧 Water
🧴 Sunscreen
🕶️ Shades
🧢 Hats
🧺 Picnic blankets
…and anything else to help you stay cool and comfortable throughout the day!

🗓️ KAMPITITION 2026
📍 TODAY | 11AM – 4PM
📌 Oakes Lower Lawn

#KAMPITITION2026 #FilipinoMythology #Sirena #Bungisngis

The countdown continues as we celebrate the legends of the Tikbalang and the Tamawo from Filipino mythology. 🇵🇭✨

The Tikbalang is a tall, mysterious creature known for its horse-like head and ability to lead travelers astray in the forests and mountains. 🐎🌫️ Often seen as both a trickster and guardian of nature, the Tikbalang remains one of the most iconic beings in Filipino folklore.

The Tamawo, originating from Visayan mythology, are enchanting spirit beings believed to live in forests, hills, and untouched lands. 🌿✨ Known for their beauty and mystical presence, they are often connected to nature, hidden realms, and ancient wisdom.

From wandering trails to hidden worlds, these legends remind us of the mystery and imagination woven throughout Filipino storytelling.

We stand with you. We will not be silent. We will not be afraid. We will continue to pray, organize, and stand for the dignity of every Muslim life.
إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وحسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل

posts.caption:
🏆 4 DAYS LEFT ‘TIL KAMPITITION 2026! 👁️🌙

As we count down to KAMPITITION 2026, we’re celebrating our theme of Filipino mythology with the Engkanto and the Aswang, while also highlighting Filipino American artists for AAPI Heritage Month! 🇵🇭✨

The Engkanto are mystical beings known for their beauty, enchantment, and deep connection to nature. They are often associated with the spirits of ancestors or the dead. It is a general term used for any human-like being! 🌿 Meanwhile, the Aswang is one of the most infamous and feared creatures in Filipino folklore! They are characterized by any shapeshifting creature, which includes vampires! 🌙👁️

For our AAPI Artist, we are spotlighting Filipino American artist, Underscores! Underscores is one of the most prominent faces of both hyper pop and electro pop, embracing individuality within their music! 🎶⚡

posts.caption:
🏆 5 DAYS LEFT ‘TIL KAMPITITION 2026! 🌊🔥

The legends are rising as we count down to KAMPITITION 2026 featuring the Santelmo and the Berkakan from Filipino mythology. 🇵🇭✨

The Santelmo, also known as Apoy ni San Elmo, is a mysterious floating fireball in Philippine folklore often believed to be the wandering soul of someone lost at sea or in remote places. 🔥 The Berkakan, from the Ilocano epic Biag ni Lam-ang, is a legendary giant sea creature feared for its immense power, swallowing even the great hero Lam-ang during his fishing journey. 🌊🐋

From blazing flames to the depths of the ocean, these legends reflect the mystery, strength, and storytelling deeply rooted in Filipino culture.

KAMPERS, are YOU ready to bring that mythical energy to KAMPITITION this Friday? 💪⚡

posts.caption:
WHAT IS CHANGEMAKERS?

Since 2004, engaging education has designed and produced programs that support the recruitment and retention of young people from historically under- resourced communities.

As part of our mission to provide a purposeful, transformative, and relevant educational experiences for all students, engaging education hosts an annual Changemakers event that features national social justice leaders.

posts.caption:
May 20th is observed in Cambodia as the National Day of Remembrance. This annual commemoration marks the Cambodian genocide that occurred under the Khmer Rouge regime between 1975 and 1979. As many of us are descendents of the genocide, it is important we remember and grieve our histories, our hardships, and our people’s stories. Please join us to honor this day on Wednesday May 20, from 6-8:30PM at Stevenson Fireside Lounge.

The event will include a historical lecture, a vigil in which we encourage people to bring offerings (flowers, food, pictures etc.) for, and food. Through this event we hope to foster a safe space for the collective grieving and honoring of those who were lost.

Scan the QR code or use the link in our linktree to RSVP.  Food will be provided

Introducing sponsors for Changemakers 2026: Student Orgs, Resource Centers, Departments, Institutes, and the Colleges!

🗓️Thursday, May 21st at 7pm
🚪Doors open at 6:30pm!
📍Location: Merrill Cultural Center
❗️RSVP in our bio/Linktree!

To kick off AAPI month, APISA is collaborating with the redwoodfreemarket on a special meal kit!! Our meal kit features a populare Samoan dish, Sapa Sui😋

Sapa Sui (SAH-PA SUE-EE) is an irresistible, comforting Samoan staple. Dark, savory, and aromatic stir-fry of vermicelli noodles, soy sauce, and tender meat. Enhanced with fragrant ginger and garlic, it is an essential, crowd-pleasing dish of Polynesian gatherings!

If you want to give it a try, please sign up for the meal kit with the link in our linktree, sign-ups close 5/4 !! DONT KNOCK IT TILL YOU TRY IT🫵🏽

The brothers of the Lethal Lambda Gamma Chapter are proud to announce the “La Fuerza” Scholarship!

This scholarship is dedicated to supporting low-income, first-generation students who are beginning their college journey at UC Santa Cruz🎓✨

We recognize that pursuing higher education can come with financial and personal challenges, especially for those who are the first in their families to attend college. La Fuerza was created to help ease that transition by providing financial support while also uplifting students who have shown resilience, determination, and a commitment to their future.

Our goal is to invest in students who will not only succeed at UCSC, but also continue to give back and make an impact in their communities.

Apply using the link in our bio or scanning the qr code. We cant wait to hear your stories! 💜

posts.caption:
Sign ups for our free BLS program are here! We are so excited to offer Basic Life Support (BLS) certification courses through the American Heart Association to UC Santa Cruz Pre-Health students at absolutely no cost.

The course consists of a single, 5-hour-long session.
Sessions will be held on Saturdays from 10 am to 3 pm.
Available dates include May 2nd, May 9th, May 16th, and May 23rd, 2026. 

Unlike some other programs, there is no online course required beforehand.

If you are selected from this form, you must make sure to accept the subsequent Google Calendar invite to secure your spot.

Located at the UCSC Police - Emergency Response Center (114 Carriage House Rd, Santa Cruz, CA 95064)

Enrollment is restricted to current UCSC students in any major and priority is given based on who signs up first and club members who attend meetings. 

If you have any questions please reach out to Elana McGrew, Free BLS Project Organizer and 25-26 Vice President of Emergency Medical Slugs, at ermcgrew@ucsc.edu.

posts.caption:
And that's a wrap on the 2026 Western Regional Bioethics Bowl! 🐌

6 dedicated students gave all of Winter quarter and the start of Spring quarter to form bioethical frameworks for 14 real life cases. On April 11th, 2026, the UCSC Bioethics Bowl Team competed against UC Davis, Cal Poly SLO, Arizona State University, and SJSU. Coming just short of a win, the team represented our school with synergy, competitive spirit, and light hearts. 

The Bioethics Club hopes to continue competing through the years, creating opportunities for students to engage in science policy, medical framework, and the human condition. 

#ucsc

Last quarter we had the amazing opportunity to compete at davisdhwani , boston.bandish , and uscmehfil . We had the most wonderful time performing and watching all the amazing and talented teams in the circuit. After countless hours of dedication of practice we are honored to have placed 3rd at USC’s Mehfil. Additionally, our very own rudy_3035 won best South Asian Soloist at Davis Dhwani for “Soona Soona”. 

We congratulate tamuswaram umd_anokha and stanfordraagapella for their placings at Davis Dhwani, purduetaal , jhu_kranti , and rutgersraag for their placings at Boston Bandish, and maizemirchi and dhunkimusic for 2nd and 1st at USC Mehfil! We loved loved watching these talented teams perform 💕

Thank you so much to all our friends and family who have supported us throughout our entire competition season and to everyone who came out to support us and watch us perform on our competition stages. We are extremely grateful for all the love and support! 

We had so much fun this competition season competing one last time with our beloved graduating seniors and for the first time with our amazing newbies and we are so very excited to be back next year with more new exciting performances! 💙💛

posts.caption:
Our club is the first and only pre-hospital emergency medicine–based organization on camous. We create social change by training our students in first aid skills and providing volunteer opportunities. We have started breaking down one of the barriers that many students face when going into medicine: gaining volunteer/clinical hours.

We provide free medical/first aid care at various UCSC events, while promoting an atmosphere of safety and community by having Slugs take care of Slugs. We also offer classes where students can get CPR certified for free.

With your contribution, we can continue to provide First Aid and Basic Life Support certification to students on campus and aid in the safety of our UCSC community.

Believing he has failed to provide the life he sacrificed his youth for, RJ clings to his family as the one thing he can still hold together. But as his loved ones look towards a future beyond their home, RJ must face the possibility that his world is moving forward without him. posts.caption:
Thursday April 2 Plastic Planet is intended as an introduction to historic
plastics in the
archaeological record
Celluloid, Bakelite, and Acrylics are all found in archaeological sites,
with artifacts dating back to the 1870s. Understanding - and even appreciating - the change that plastics as a material culture makes on the archaeological record is critical for understanding the changes to consumer behaviors. A limited survey of plastic artifacts from collections in California hints at the rise in plastic production beginning in the late-19” century, a trend that would ramp up to full gear over the next 50 years. Shaped by the plastics industry, consumer behavior turned away from traditional materials towards cheaper, more disposable, and more toxic plastic products. Knowing this history also connects the past with our current plastic pollution crisis. Discussion of Southern Oregon University’s upcoming Historic Plastics Digital Collection will also be presented and a small display from the plastic type collection will be available to handle.

What is local food? 
Student voices matter! Completing this survey takes us one step closer to changing the food you eat in the dining halls. Take 5-7 minutes out of your day, on the bus, in passing, to complete this survey on local food. How do you define local food? What metrics go into it, and do you want to see more local food in our dining halls?
Filling out this survey supports student research at UCSC and ensures we have a say in our institutional purchasing, as well as how we fuel our bodies. 
For students and by students, we can be the cause of change.

⏳ Recruiting for investment banking in the U.S. moves early, and competition is intense.

Many candidates prepare hard, but still struggle because they:
– Lack structure in technical and behavioral answers
– Underestimate the importance of networking and coffee chats
– Don’t fully understand what interviewers assess in early rounds
– Make avoidable mistakes under pressure

SelfCapital Network was built by former investment bankers to bring focused, practical preparation into one place - so you can fix those gaps early.

⚡️Inside the platform:
– Questions written and reviewed by former investment bankers
– Realistic mock interview practice with structured feedback on content & delivery
– Case-style scenarios that test how you think and your attention to detail
– Structured CV guidance and optional 1:1 support

If you’re aiming for internships, or full-time roles, preparation starts earlier than you think

👉 selfcapitalnetwork.com

Ever wondered how we turn thousands of messy neural signals into a clean, controllable BCI command? It all starts with Data Manipulation & PCA.

Join us this Friday for a deep dive into dimensionality reduction. We’re breaking down how to find the "latent dynamics" of the brain and separate meaningful neural patterns from the background hum.

#NeuroTech #UCSC #BCI #DataScience #NeuralEngineering #PCA #SlugLife

posts.caption:
3, 2, 1… liftoff! 🚀 UC Santa Cruz students got a front-row view of a weather balloon launch at East Field during the UC Santa Cruz premier hackathon, @cruzhacks. 

Developed by CruzHacks sponsor WindBorne, these lightweight helium balloons carry sensors that collect precise weather data to improve forecasting.

Students got an up-close look at the equipment, learned about the application programming interface (API) behind the system, and even helped deploy the balloon into the sky.

The launch also gave students a chance to interact directly with industry partners and see how classroom concepts translate to real-world applications.

This activity highlights UCSC and CruzHacks’ focus on using engineering and innovation to advance sustainability and climate solutions 🌎✨

posts.caption: This weekend I was able to take down the 2026 New Years Classic🎆🎆🏆!!! Super fun tournament at Chabot, a course which I had only played once before. The weather was pretty crazy all weekend, with wind on Saturday and some heavy rain on Sunday, but I had a blast all the same! As for my game, it felt solid for the most part, with a few shaky putts and mistakes down the stretch to make for an awesome battle with @lewdawg51242! I was able to secure the win in a playoff with a nice 420 foot park job on hole 1. Overall, I’m happy with how my game is feeling going into 2026 and I’m excited to see what I can bring to the field this season! Shoutout my sponsor, @mvpdiscsports for the awesome discs, the Terra and Timelapse were putting in work this weekend!

📢 ALAY IS NOW ACCEPTING WRITTEN AND/OR VISUAL ART SUBMISSIONS FOR VOL. 30 OF OUR ANNUAL ANTHOLOGY: PAGKABATA! ⟡ ݁₊ . 📢

to submit your work, you can either:
1. scan the QR CODE in this post!
2. visit the LINKTREE in our bio!
3. typing “ tinyurl.com/alay30 “ in your search bar!

the slides for our THEME REVEAL will be accessible through our linktree as well!

────୨ৎ────

- what are pieces of advice you would like to offer to your younger self?
- what are ways you can (re)connect with your inner child?
- how do you embrace youth?

────୨ৎ────

With the ‘25 - ‘26 theme, PAGKABATA, or “childhood”, it aims to give an opportunity for people to embrace youth with ourselves and with others, especially in a world that constantly pushes us to be adults.

ᯓ what does “PAGKABATA” mean to YOU?★

────୨ৎ────

submissions are due FEBRUARY 28th @ 11:59PM! we can’t wait to see your contributions! 𐔌՞ ܸ.ˬ.ܸ՞𐦯

🌎 Introducing our GIS Day expert speaker panel! 🎤

Friday, Nov. 21st from 2-5pm at the Namaste Lounge, professionals in research, industry, and government comprise our guests who will be speaking on “GIS In Action,” sharing how GIS shapes our world! 💬

Learn from:
🐾 Dr. Chris Wilmers, Professor in Environmental Studied here at UCSC. Head of the Wilmers Lab on wildlife ecology at UCSC and leading the Santa Cruz Puma Project. 

🚀 Dr. Shadi Oveisgharan, scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and esteemed researcher in remote sensing and radar science. 

🌐 Dr. Jon Detka, NASA Ames researcher and faculty at CSU Monterey Bay, studying remote sensing and Earth observation.

🥼 John Haskins, water quality monitoring scientist at the Elkhorn Slough Reserve. 

Join us to learn more from professionals in the field, network, and celebrate the wonders of GIS! 🛰️

#ucsc #ucsantacruz #expertpanel #gis #industryprofessionals

Come celebrate international GIS Week with:
📣 - Student Map Competition!! ($200 prizes!)
🎤 - Expert speaker panel! (to be released!)
🌎 - GeoQuest Trivia!
🥨 - Free snacks and networking :) 

So… what is GIS?? Ever wonder how maps tell us stories about our world? From tracking wildlife to mapping climate data, GIS (Geographic Information Systems) helps us see the intricate connections between people, places, and the planet!! 🗺️

Whether you’re deep into mapping or just curious and exploring, GIS Day is the perfect place to connect, learn, and get inspired! 💡 Hope to see you all there!! 

Jointly hosted by GISTAR, CISR, and the Drone & GIS Society at UCSC! 🛰️

On the behalf of ΣMΔ, the brothers would like to extend a huge congratulations to Dr. Pablo Alvarez of the Xi Class on completing his PhD dissertation!!! 🦠

“My dissertation is all about how different viruses overcome the barriers our body uses to defend itself. From this work, we can develop novel vaccines, antivirals, diagnostics, and even design gene therapy vectors. Sigma Mu Delta has provided nothing but an amazing supportive network that jumpstarted my career in science and biomedical research!”

From finishing his undergrad at UCSC in 2020, Dr. Alvarez continued his post-grad at UCLA as a PhD Candidate with a focus on Microbiology and Immunology.

Prevailing Together, Gamma Chapter⚕️

#postgraduate #ucsc #ucla

posts.caption:
亲爱的Slugs们大家好！૮(˶ᵔ ᵕ ᵔ˶)ა
即日起至10月7日 到10月18日，UCSC - CSSA（中国学生学者联合会/Chinese Students and Scholars Association）的招新活动周正式开启！
期待能在未来的日子里，与CSSA共同成长、互相成就！

本次招新旨在招募以下岗位：
宣传部
 - 摄影
 - 剪辑
 - 文案（管理社交媒体账号）
 - 封面，海报设计
策划部
 -策划部部员
财务部
 -财务部成员

CSSA各部门简介
📍宣传部：
宣传部主要负责运营和更新cssa的社交媒体账号，宣传海报制作，活动拍摄记录，记录各种大小活动并进行图文宣发及回顾等
📍策划部：
策划部主要负责社团活动的计划与举办，前期会有关于活动计划的会议，后期在活动当天也负责摆设清场和驻场的工作人员等。
📍财务部：
财务的主要职责包括管理和分配资金、审核各部门活动预算及支出、监督CSSA各个平台资金、保证财务记录的准确性。此外还需配合其他部门，积极与策划部沟通活动预算开支，与公关部协同处理公关合作进账，和主席与副主席共同讨论组织未来发展事项。

此次面试为线上，欢迎大家填写以下Google Form报名并预约面试，我们会在报名后2-3个工作日发送您具体的面试时间～～现在参与筹备将会参与10月-11月正在预热中的狼人杀万圣节活动，有超高经验且感兴趣的小伙伴我们期待你的到来！
Google Form：https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdNhfuWgKytcRIJQ5Q7NvtKSI3YPCPHr5m0q9j5Mbqnvm3vlQ/viewform?usp=dialog
#ucsccssa #ucsc #ucscchinseprogram

Today we are grateful that survivors and their families can work towards healing and reconnecting.

Introducing our 2025-26 IGC Executive Vice President!!

Hi everyone! My name is Mads Bobele, and I’m absolutely thrilled to serve as the 2025–26 IGC Executive Vice President!
I joined Kappa Alpha Theta as a transfer student last fall and stepped into the role of my chapter’s IGC delegate during winter quarter. From my very first meeting, I knew I’d found something special. I genuinely loved being part of the IGC community, which is why I’m so excited to take on this new position and continue supporting and connecting our incredible chapters. I’m a fourth year literature major with dreams of becoming a teacher one day. When I’m not buried in books, you’ll probably find me on a beach drive with friends, grabbing coffee or lunch with my sisters, or diving into a good romance series. I can’t wait to see all that we accomplish together this year and to get to know even more of you along the way. Let’s make it a great year!

May 14th is Hmong American Day! 🩷

Hmong people are an ethnic group from Laos who were affected by the Vietnam War which caused them to flee to countries like the United States, France, Australia, and more. Today, there are well known communities in Fresno, CA and Minnesota.

posts.caption:
শুভ বসন্ত! Shuvo Boshonto! 🌼

A few clicks from our celebration of Pohela Falgun. Thank you to everyone who were able to join us!

Falgun is the eleventh month in the Bangla calendar and the first month of the season, spring (Boshonto). Pohela Falgun is the first day of spring. With colourful attire, flowers and songs Pohela Falgun is traditionally celebrated. The festival started in the Bangla calendar year 1401, since then, Pohela Falgun has been celebrated every year.

Dear UCSC students, faculty and friends 

Spring festival is the most important traditional festival in Chinese culture, and it is a wonderful time for family reunion, saying goodbye to the old and welcoming the new. In order to celebrate this meaningful festival with you, we sincerely invite you to attend the UCSC Spring Festival Gala.

This party will present you with a cultural feast that combines tradition and modernity. We will have wonderful cultural performances by UCSC students and fun interactive games that will bring you joy and surprises; we have also prepared hot dumplings 🥟 and various snacks 🍬 for all of you. 

Registration: Free of charge, scan the QR code below to register.

 We look forward to spending this wonderful evening with you and welcoming the New Year together!
 All the best for the new year!

 ✨ Time: Saturday, January 25, 2025 at 6:00pm
 ✨ Where: Stevenson Event Center
 🎊 UCSC CSSA respectfully invites 🎊

CSSA 2025 Spring Festival:Call for Performances & Volunteers

🌟 Join Us for the Celebration! 🌟
The Spring Festival is coming, and we’re looking for talented individuals and dedicated volunteers to make this year’s event unforgettable!

Program Information
What: Any type of performance is welcome! Singing, dancing, comedy, magic tricks, traditional Chinese art, poetry recitals, and more—show us your creativity and talent!
Who: Everyone is invited to participate! Whether you’re a student, a teacher, or a community member, this is your chance to shine on stage. 

Volunteer Opportunities
If performing isn’t your thing, join our team of volunteers! Roles include:
Event planning and coordination
Stage management
Tech and audio-visual support
Decoration and set design
Audience coordination
How to Sign Up:
📎Link：https://forms.gle/kVGVZs4mAd2HKiwS7

Don’t miss this chance to be part of an exciting and memorable event!

Let’s celebrate the joy of the Spring Festival together! 🌸🎉

2024CSSA秋招已经开启📣('ᴗ' )و欢迎扫码进群了解详情信息

本次招新旨在招募以下岗位：
公关部
-公关部部员
宣传部
-宣传部部员（特招-摄像、剪辑、文案）
策划部
-策划部部员
财务部
-财务小助手

CSSA各部门简介
📍公关部：
公关部主要负责对接与CSSA合作的校内/校外组织，主要需要做的工作包括谈线上/线下客户和资料整理。简单来说就是给CSSA挣钱！搞钱！！！
如果你是一个e人，或者对销售相关的工作内容感兴趣，或者很善于沟通，演讲（中文英文都强烈欢迎！）那么公关部是你的不二之选。如果比较内向或者只是想体验相关类型的工作也强烈欢迎加入，我们也有很多给i人的同样重要的工作机会！
欢迎大家报名加入公关部ଘ(੭ˊᵕˋ)੭* ੈ✩‧₊˚
📍宣传部：
宣传部主要负责运营和更新cssa的社交媒体账号，其次是负责记录各种大小活动并进行图文宣发及回顾等
📍策划部：
策划部主要负责社团活动的计划与举办，前期会有关于活动计划的会议，后期在活动当天也负责摆设清场和驻场的工作人员等。
📍财务助手：
财务助手的主要职责包括管理和分配资金、审核各部门活动预算及支出、监督CSSA各个平台资金、保证财务记录的准确性。此外还需配合其他部门，积极与策划部沟通活动预算开支，与公关部协同处理公关合作进账，和主席与副主席共同讨论组织未来发展事项。

✨We have exciting news!✨ Sankofa Sky Farm will be at the upcoming ‘Water Fair’ event at the Monterey Bay Sanctuary Exploration Center on Friday, April 19th 2024 from 11am - 3pm. This event will be hosted by UCSC and Monterey Bay Sanctuary Exploration Center.

RSVP is NOT required!‼️

💡Do you know where your water comes from? How often do you visit the beach? Looking at an orange sunset ocean view or a crystal clear blue lake water is breathtaking. It is the source of life. A precious resource we tend to take for granted. Here in Santa Cruz it is a unique place with both surrounding forests and ocean coastlines. Our city is magical. As residents it is our responsibility to understand how to protect and steward the natural resources that create our beautiful home.

💧If you want to learn more about Santa Cruz water systems, this event will include informational poster sessions from UCSC student researchers, art activities, local organizations, and educational games for all ages! Sankofa Sky Farm will be showcasing our atmospheric water generator prototype, you don’t want to miss it!🤍

posts.caption:
Hello everyone! We are so excited to introduce you all to Sankofa Sky Farm! 🌱

Sankofa Sky Farm (SSF) is a student-led vertical farming research project at UCSC that aims to revolutionize sustainable agriculture.

💡This project was founded by current UCSC Agroecology student, Sheyna Burns. When asked about what inspired her to start SSF, Burns states, “The driving force behind Sankofa Sky Farm was a basic need: access. This need centers on ensuring everyone can get healthy, nutrient-packed produce regardless of where they live or how much money they have—it’s a basic human right.”

Swipe to check out our Q&A with Sheyna, and to learn about our mission, visions, and much more! ➡️

Special thank you to our faculty and staff sponsors for their generous support, and thank you to our wonderful first cohort of students for their hard work and dedication!

If you would like to get involved, please visit the link in our bio, or you may email Sheyna Burns at shaburns@ucsc.edu

✨Follow @ucsc.sankofaskyfarm to stay in touch with us!

posts.caption:
Hi grads,

We’ve got a new potential workshop series we’re thinking of hosting! We’re trying to get student feedback on whether this reformed workshop style is needed, and how to design it to make it the most useful for graduate students. If you want to provide this feedback, please fill out the google form (link in bio) by Feb 23rd. Thank you!!!

Overview: The proposed workshop series aims to expand upon the traditional “What I Wish I Knew” (WIWIK) format by addressing the “hidden curriculum” of graduate school with a more comprehensive approach made up of 3 key components:
Part 1: Informational (discuss what you need to know about the topic)
Part 2: Example (graduate student lead(s) will show an example of what is discussed in part 1)
Part 3: Student support (graduate student lead(s) will help workshop attendees with practicing/writing/etc content discussed in prior parts and give feedback to provide actionable student support)

posts.caption: Start clutching your pearls, because we’re taking a deep dive into some of cinema’s most explicit and daring endeavors! This February, Film Society brings to you our first theme to launch the club: History of the X-Rating! Each Sunday throughout the month, we’ll screen a new film to represent the long and detailed history of the X rating and censorship in Hollywood. Featuring: John Schlesinger’s Best Picture-winning tale that brought explicit content to the mainstream, Ken Russell’s hellish & horny spectacle of sacrilege, Lucio Fulci’s lovecraftian video nasty “beyond” your wildest nightmares, and John Cameron Mitchell’s refreshingly raw exploration of queer sex & romance in the NYC underground. Mark your calendars for each Sunday in February - the location and time for next week’s screening will be posted shortly!

Giving Day is November 8th, and WiPA is raising funds so we can continue to provide our events/programs to the physics community! These events include things like our weekly meetings, annual events, guest speakers, and support for BIPOC, WOC, transgender and gender non-conforming students in STEM. WiPA is a student-led group that strives to bring individuals together to work towards a more diverse community in physics and astronomy. 

This year, we are participating in two challenges, the Night Owl (12:00am-1:00am) and the Mid-Day Motivator (12:00pm-2:00pm). During these times, the amount of donors will count most, not the amount of money. Groups with the largest number of donors will receive bonus funds! Any gifts are sincerely appreciated. Your contribution will ensure the ongoing delivery of our programs/events, develop a supportive culture in physics and astronomy, and help us all succeed. Every gift makes a difference. Thank you!

posts.caption:
We are the PBSE Graduate Student Council! Founded in 2020 by Donna Poscablo, the PBSE Grad Council has a goal of creating a diverse, inclusive, and equitable research training environment for graduate students in PBSE. Student representatives and faculty members on the council work together to develop long-term policy and event-based solutions to problems facing graduate students and departments. The overarching goal of this council is to address the gaps in PBSE to ensure a fulfilling, productive, and successful experience at UCSC. If you want to learn more about the PBSE Council, please visit our website (link in bio). If you have an idea for improving graduate students' experience in PBSE, or you want to help us plan events, please email our Google Group @pbsegradcouncil-group@ucsc.edu. 

Also, we are hoping to highlight and uplift graduate student successes on our website and Insta! These can take the form of getting a grant, publishing a paper, learning a new technique, or anything you are excited to share with the grad community. Feel free to DM us or check out the form on our website to be highlighted! We look forward to connecting and building the PBSE community! Please feel free to reach out if you are interested in getting involved too! 

Beautiful logo design creds to Fran, our CB3 rep! ✨

posts.caption:
In life, we get caught up in all the things that we are told make us happy; whether that be that new job, next iPhone, or even a romantic partner.

If we try to be happy solely by obtaining these things, then we'll live a life of chasing and not a life of enjoying. Always make sure to sit down, meditate, and find enjoyment within yourself. A happy mind will lead to a happy life 😊

#happiness #meditation #lifeadvice #artofliving #mentalhealth #innerpeace

posts.caption:
🤘🏼FIRST OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT🤘🏼

Welcome to UCSC Skimboard Club! This is our first official year and we are stoked to get it rolling! Due to COVID we will not start in-person events until Spring Quarter, but in the meantime we will be hosting virtual meetings over zoom to anyone who is interested in being apart of what we are trying to build here which is a club dedicated to everything skim-boarding and meeting others who share this interest.  Even if you can’t skimboard we welcome you with open arms! We are more than happy to teach you and even if it’s not your thing you are always welcome to kick it with us at the beach.  We are looking to try and host socials sometime this Spring Quarter (if COVID has been contained) or next Fall Quarter.  A quick shootout to Elijah (@solowohashi) who designed our sweet logo, we will start rolling out club gear sometime in the Winter or Spring so keep your eyes peeled for future announcements.  If you are interested in being a member please email us and we will add you to our list.  We will also be creating a discord in the winter for the club where members can let others know if they are skimming in the area.  If you have any questions feel free to email us we are pretty responsive.  Stay psyched!

to our pre-law followers,
now more than ever is a time to reflect on the difference between legal and right, and how the justice system produces inequitable outcomes.  it is the time to think critically about your legal pathway and the impact your work can have on others.  it is not the time to be afraid to protest or advocate for #blm lest law schools find it “unprofessional.” your silence right now is a failure to advocate for rights, rights disproportionally denied to Black people.  if any of the above statements offend you, please reflect on why you are pursuing a career in law.
